title: OPERATION HUNGRY GROUND
situation:
When the Word of Blake garrison abandoned {WORLD} in {YEAR}, it spent its last six hours of air cover poisoning the Carseland floodplain. That floodplain is 11,400 hectares of grain land, and it is the only grain land the northern hemisphere has. The Blakists seeded it with chemical canisters. The coalition survey calls the poison SABLE RAIN. It kills on contact and stays deadly in wet soil for about 30 months. The provincial assembly at {DISTRICT} voted three times to make relief a priority but paid for it only once. That money bought your unit, {CLEAR_TEAMS} certified clearance teams, and one warehouse of antidote injectors. {EMPLOYER} wants you to guard the clearance work and speed it up, certify at least 6,200 hectares as clean before the planting window closes, and hold the exclusion line until then.

The deadline comes from the river, not from politics. The Carse floods every winter. The water went down 9 days ago, and crops can only be sown within {PLANT_WINDOW} days of that. Miss the window and there is no growing season, and no food for 900,000 people. Each team clears 14 to 22 hectares a day, depending on how thickly the canisters were laid. That does not reach 6,200 hectares in time. To close the gap you need either more workers or more risk, and the assembly has twice refused to vote on which.

The hard ground is the levees. The Carseland Levees are the only ground in the floodplain that can carry anything over 40 tons. Everything off the levee tops is waterlogged rice paddy that bogs down vehicles and traps the poison in the root mat. The Blakists knew this, so they seeded the levee tops four times as heavily as the fields. Your 'Mechs can only watch over the flats from the levees, but the levees have to be cleared first. The clearance teams want your 'Mechs watching before they walk the levee tops. So one side has to go first, unprotected.

Three more facts. First, the people are not waiting. Their food covers 40 days at three-quarter rations, and at night they cross the tape to scavenge seed grain and salvage. In the first 19 days, 31 died and 64 were poisoned (from the district medical registry, three days old). Second, cleared plots are not staying clean. Someone has re-seeded canisters on 4 plots you already certified, all within 800 meters of the Blackbottom drainage cuts. The pattern points to a stay-behind team of 6 to 10 people with at least one small boat, though this is unconfirmed. Third, the poison-density map your whole schedule depends on came from a Blakist deserter handled by {NPC:intel-source}. It is nine days old. So far it has been right about every levee but wrong about two of the five field grids, so assume it stays two-fifths wrong.

The injectors are the resource nobody votes on. You have {INJECTOR_STOCK} doses, resupply is 60 days away, and every casualty draws from the same shelf, whether soldier, clearance tech, or scavenger.

objectives.primary: Certify 6,200 hectares of the Carseland floodplain clean, levee tops included, before the planting window closes {PLANT_WINDOW} days after the flood went down.
objectives.secondary: Find and stop the team re-seeding poison from the Blackbottom drainage cuts. After day 20, no certified plot gets poisoned again.
objectives.bonus: Train and equip a local clearance corps to coalition standard so the work continues after your contract ends.

complications.name: The Map Is Two-Fifths Wrong
complications.text: The deserter's poison-density map sets the clearance schedule, but it is wrong on 40 percent of the field grids. Nobody finds out a grid is wrong until a team is already standing in it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: When a team opens a new field grid, roll for map accuracy. A wrong grid cuts that team's daily rate in half and forces a one-day re-survey before certification can start again.

complications.name: Scavengers
complications.text: Hungry people cross the tape at night, on paths they know, to reach seed grain your teams have not cleared yet. Whether or not they are your responsibility, they become your casualties.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On any night with no dedicated tape patrols, a civilian casualty event occurs. It draws 2-8 injectors from stock and costs the nearest clearance team its next morning for recovery and decontamination.

complications.name: The Injector Shelf
complications.text: One stock of antidote serves everyone inside the exclusion line. The medical annex is clear: below 300 doses, clearance slows to half speed by standing order. Clearing poison without a reserve of antidote just makes more casualties.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Track injector stock as a campaign resource. Below 300 doses, all clearance rates drop by half. At zero, clearance stops entirely until resupply on day 60.

complications.name: Soft Ground
complications.text: Off the levee tops, the rice paddy bogs down anything heavy and holds poison in the root mat. Pulling out a bogged vehicle is hard enough on its own, and the mud is poisoned too.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Vehicles over 40 tons must stay on the levee tops. 'Mechs off the tops roll a bog check each turn of sustained movement. Any recovery in poisoned paddy costs a full decontamination cycle and 4-6 injectors held in reserve.

decisionPoints.name: Whose Hands
decisionPoints.context: The certified teams alone cannot clear 6,200 hectares before the planting window closes. There are three ways to close the gap, and the assembly has refused to pick one.

options.title: Certified Teams Only
advantages: The lowest casualty rate of any way to do the work
Every cleared plot is properly certified and can be defended later
No political risk with the assembly
disadvantages: You still fall short by an estimated 1,400 to 2,200 hectares
That shortfall becomes a 14-month food deficit
As uncleared land stays uncleared, more scavengers cross the tape
options.consequence: You keep professional standards, but the harvest pays for it. The shortfall shows up first as missing grain, then as smaller rations, then as deaths in the spring records.

costs.resource: harvest shortfall: 1,400-2,200 hectares left unplanted for 14 months
costs.risk: the food shortage becomes next winter's emergency, with your unit's name on the certification record

options.title: Paid Volunteer Corps
advantages: Closes the gap with 200 to 300 local workers at 14 C-bills a day
Those workers know the drainage cuts and the scavenger paths
The assembly's farm bloc backs it loudly
disadvantages: Volunteers get killed 3 to 5 times as often as certified teams do
Every casualty drains the same injector shelf and the same political goodwill
Training the volunteers costs the certified teams 6 working days up front
options.consequence: The land gets cleared, and the price is paid locally, a little at a time, at funerals the assembly members attend.

costs.resource: injectors burn twice as fast for as long as the program runs
costs.risk: one bad day with many volunteer deaths ends both the program and the assembly's support

options.title: Blakist Prisoner Labor
advantages: Among 240 prisoners of war, 31 are trained combat engineers, the fastest hands you have
It costs nothing from the relief budget
It closes the gap with 9 to 12 days to spare
disadvantages: The rules are clear: dangerous work by prisoners needs their consent, and that consent vanishes after the first death
Count on sabotage from inside the labor force, and plan for it
The first prisoner killed by his own side's poison becomes propaganda for both sides at once
options.consequence: The people who poisoned the ground are the ones who clear it. Every other consequence lands later, by committee, by broadcast, and in the next contract's terms.

costs.resource: 1 platoon tied up guarding prisoners for the whole program
costs.risk: one sabotage or revenge incident turns the relief program into a war-crimes inquiry, with your unit on the record as the jailer

decisionPoints.name: The Boat in the Cuts
decisionPoints.context: The re-seeding team works from the Blackbottom drainage cuts at night. Every plot it poisons is a plot you already paid to clear.

options.title: Night Ambush Program
advantages: Stops the problem at its source if you catch the team
The cuts are a narrow approach, which makes for a good ambush
A captured re-seeder is your best lead on the remaining poison caches
disadvantages: Your best infantry leaves the tape to run it, so scavenger deaths rise on those nights
The team shows up every 3 to 6 days at random, so expect 2 to 3 empty weeks of waiting
Night fighting on poisoned ground means fighting in full protective gear, half-blind
options.consequence: Pulling infantry off the tape to watch the cuts thins your patrols elsewhere. You trade a known nightly risk to scavengers for an uncertain chance of catching the team in one clean fight.

costs.resource: tape patrol coverage drops 40 percent on ambush nights; expect about one extra civilian casualty event per week
costs.risk: a firefight on poisoned ground in protective gear; friendly casualties draw 10-15 injectors in one night

options.title: Weekly Re-Survey
advantages: Every certified plot is re-checked weekly, so no farmer walks onto a re-seeded plot thinking it is clean
No fighting, just careful work
It also catches map errors as a bonus
disadvantages: Clearance slows 20 percent for the whole program, so the gap reopens
The re-seeding team keeps the upper hand for as long as this lasts
Teams re-checking ground they think is clean get careless, and careless is how certification fails
options.consequence: The program soaks up the attacks instead of stopping them. It is safe and slow, but the 20 percent slowdown reopens the shortfall problem from another angle.

costs.resource: clearance rate drops 20 percent; 900-1,300 hectares of your time margin spent on re-checking
costs.risk: the team steps up and starts poisoning the levee tops behind your watch pattern

options.title: Grate the Drainage Cuts
advantages: Blocks the boat for good, and it is built once instead of patrolled nightly
Frees your infantry for the tape once it is done
It is sturdy, plain to see, and cheap to keep up
disadvantages: 6 engineering days at three cut mouths, working in poisoned water
Blocking the cuts backs up the field drains for two villages, waterlogging 380 hectares of your target into next season
The team switches to coming in overland; slower for them, but the threat changes rather than ends
options.consequence: The cuts close and the water backs up elsewhere. The two flooded villages will be told it was the cheaper choice. That is true, and it will not comfort them.

costs.resource: 380 hectares of your target lost to flooding
costs.risk: political: two village delegations show up at the assembly mid-program, with the farm bloc listening

entries.event: A blast or a poisoning on a certified plot: re-seeding is confirmed in the grid you are working.
You send a medical and decontamination team; the injectors they use are logged against your stock.
The plot loses its clean rating; nearby grids pause for re-check. Clearance teams hold at the tape.
Re-check of the poisoned plot is done, at the cost of one team-day against the window.
The district registry publishes the casualty. Scavengers shift to grids they think are untouched, and the assembly puts off its questions to the next sitting.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The planting window closes {PLANT_WINDOW} days after the flood goes down. Every hectare not certified by that morning stays unplanted for 14 months. The northern hemisphere's food count is based on what your teams actually certified, not on what they tried or what the assembly voted for.

opforSketch.composition: Word of Blake stay-behind re-seeding team: 6-10 effectives (Veteran), one shallow-draft boat, man-portable canister stocks cached in the drainage network. Secondary contact volume from armed scavenger bands (Green, 4-12 per band, smallarms only) working the exclusion zone's edges. Generator should keep direct combat rare and small; the threat is to the program, not the unit.
opforSketch.behavior: The team avoids all contact and attacks certification itself: re-seeds by night, observes response patterns, and will mine a levee crown if 'Mech overwatch settles into routine. Scavengers flee from force and return behind it. Nobody on the other side wants your battle; they want your schedule.

forks.name: OPERATION SEED CORN
forks.trigger: 6,200+ hectares certified inside the window; re-seeding interdicted.
forks.consequence: The crop goes in, and the harvest becomes the district's strategic asset — and target. The unit is offered the follow-on garrison contract: granaries, levee patrol lines, and the first harvest convoys under guard.

forks.name: OPERATION EMPTY BOWL
forks.trigger: Certified acreage falls short by 1,000 hectares or more, or clearance suspends on a dry injector shelf.
forks.consequence: Ration issue drops to half by mid-winter. The district food offices come under crowd pressure on a published schedule — issue days — and the unit still under contract becomes the line between the queue and the warehouse.

forks.name: OPERATION GLASS HOUSE
forks.trigger: A prisoner-labor incident, volunteer mass-casualty day, or gleaner shooting at the tape becomes an assembly inquiry.
forks.consequence: An inquiry commission arrives with subpoena power over the unit's logs while the clearance program continues around it. The unit guards the commission, its records, and its witnesses — having become, in part, the subject.

storyElementSeed: A clearance tech kneels at the flag line, lifts a canister the size of a thermos with two fingers and a held breath, and sets it in the sand box. Behind the tape a farmer watches the row she is not yet allowed to plant and counts days on her fingers.

merc.situation.framing: Read clause 9 before the first boot crosses the tape. Your unit is liable for any poisoning inside the exclusion line, scavengers included. The real treasure on this contract is the injector shelf: C-bills arrive by wire transfer, but antidote takes 60 days to resupply, and the employer's relief committee has never had to stand downwind of either problem.

resourceGates.lackingText: Without depot engineering stocks such as flail rigs and spare protective suits, certified-team rates drop from 14-22 to 9-14 hectares per day, and the projected shortfall grows to 2,400-3,200 hectares.

skeleton: clearance force must certify poisoned cropland against an immovable planting date while the hungry population enters the ground faster than it is cleared and a night team re-seeds what the day certified
inspiration: post-liberation agricultural demining, France 1945-46, including the POW-labor controversy

title: OPERATION SEALED REGISTER
situation:
The Blessed Order's compound above {DISTRICT} on {WORLD} was retaken in {YEAR} with its transmission floor intact, which the after-action summary called good luck. The summary said little about what sits two levels below that floor: the district ROM registry, called the Register. It holds {FILE_COUNT} informer and case files covering 11 Protectorate worlds. Who informed. Who was paid. Who was forced to sign but signed anyway. Who wore ComStar white but worked for the Word of Blake from day one. A coalition commission lands in {COMMISSION_DAYS} days to take the files and judge them. Until its custody officer signs for them, your detail holds the vault. And every survivor of the schism wants to know what the vault says about everyone else.

You face four threats. First, the retreating staff rigged the vault to burn. There are 31 thermite charges, set to fire either on command or if anyone tampers with them, and the staff drained the fire-suppression lines before they left. Only one man knows how to disarm it: the captured Custodian-Adept, held under guard in the compound and now bargaining. Second, a Word of Blake remnant cell is still in the city below, an estimated 12 to 20 fighters, from intelligence six days old. The Register names their stay-behind network, so their job is to destroy it. Two probing attacks on the vehicle ramp in nine days fit that theory. Third, the petitioners: a camp of {PETITIONERS} people has grown on the Procession Stair, families of the disappeared whose files are inside, adding 40 to 80 more with every new rumor. Fourth, and stated plainly because the Order owes itself honesty, the Order is split. One faction wants the Register sealed and handed over untouched. Another wants it opened now and read aloud, to clear the Order's name by naming the traitors. Both factions have followers inside this compound. And 14 of your own guards served on worlds the Register covers. Nobody has read their files. That is the only neutrality left here, and one locked door protects it.

The hard ground is the Stair. The compound sits on a rocky hill above the city. Only two routes reach it: one vehicle ramp that switchbacks up the north face, and the Procession Stair on the south, 1,100 steps that a crowd can climb but no vehicle can. You cannot simply close the Stair, because its midpoint landing holds the cistern the petitioners' camp drinks from. Cut off water to 800 civilians and 11 worlds will know by the end of the week. Meanwhile the transmission floor has to keep relaying coalition traffic. The interdiction was only just lifted, and theater command logs every hour it goes dark. You are holding a relay, a vault, a prisoner, a crowd, and a roster, and the commission's signature is {COMMISSION_DAYS} days away.

objectives.primary: Hand the Register to the commission complete and unread, with the chain of custody unbroken, on the day its custody officer signs for it.
objectives.secondary: Keep the transmission floor passing coalition traffic, with total downtime under 4 hours for the whole holding period.
objectives.bonus: Disarm the thermite charges completely before the commission lands, without granting the Custodian-Adept the immunity he wants.

complications.name: The Charges
complications.text: Thirty-one thermite charges, set to fire if tampered with, and the fire-suppression lines are drained. Any unauthorized entry starts a 90-second arming cycle that only the disarm sequence can stop. The trap that guards the vault can also destroy it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any breach of the vault perimeter, whether hostile, accidental, or friendly but unauthorized, starts a 90-second clock. If no one with disarm authority reaches the vault floor in time, the Register burns and the primary objective fails for good.

complications.name: Fourteen Names
complications.text: Fourteen of your guards may have files in the drawers they guard. No one has read them, and the whole arrangement holds because no one has. Every rumor of a leak tests that.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Guards posted near the vault roll morale and loyalty checks after any leak event or approach by the faction that wants the files opened. A failed check produces an access irregularity the GM resolves: an error, a confession, or an attempt to reach the files.

complications.name: The Stair and the Cistern
complications.text: The Stair brings crowds up, and you cannot close it without cutting the camp's water. The camp is grieving families in a line, and by the second retelling a rumor becomes fact to them.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Crowd events come up the Stair and grow with each rumor cycle. Closing the Stair triggers a humanitarian crisis within 48 hours: the commission censures you, the open-the-files faction gains recruits, and the crowd doubles.

complications.name: The Transmission Floor
complications.text: The relay has to keep running. It ties up 40 percent of compound power and one of your sections around the clock, and theater command checks the uptime log before it reads your reports.
complications.mechanicalEffect: One section and 40 percent of power stay committed to the relay. You may pull them for a crisis, but each hour counts as logged downtime against the 4-hour secondary-objective limit.

decisionPoints.name: The Custodian's Price
decisionPoints.context: He will disarm the charges in exchange for passage off-world and immunity from the commission. He built the trap, he knows exactly how many days you have, and he bargains like a man reading your calendar over your shoulder.

options.title: Take the Deal
advantages: The one man who knows the sequence disarms the charges
Vault risk drops to ordinary security risk for the rest of the days
His debriefing reveals the cell's support network, at medium reliability
disadvantages: The commission's clearest case walks free, with your signature on the release
The petitioners' camp will find out, because the Stair hears everything, and your neutrality suffers
Every future custodian on 11 worlds learns that rigging an archive buys a way out
options.consequence: The Register survives to convict the whole network, but its keeper goes free. The trade makes sense on paper, yet the camp on the Stair will never accept it, and they are right to feel that way.

costs.resource: political cost: you give up the commission's flagship case before it even lands
costs.risk: the deal leaks to the Stair before the transfer, and a crowd surge hits his departure convoy

options.title: Disarm It Without Him
advantages: You concede nothing; the Custodian-Adept faces the commission for everything he did
Coalition engineers put the odds of a safe disarm at 60 percent, over a 6-hour work window
Success ends both the trap and the bargaining
disadvantages: The 40 percent chance of failure means losing the Register, which is the whole mission, for good
Six hours of work on the vault floor is six hours when the cell can try to force the charges
The suppression lines are drained, so once the thermite starts, nothing can stop it
options.consequence: The Order keeps its integrity and bets the archive on the engineers' 60 percent odds. Win or lose, rigging an archive no longer buys a way out, and no custodian gets to bargain like this again.

costs.resource: a 6-hour disarm window during which you cannot both defend the vault and work in it
costs.risk: 40 percent chance the Register burns by your own hands, handing the cell exactly what it wanted

options.title: Carry It Out Under the Array
advantages: Takes the prize out of the trap without disturbing the trap
Hand-carry teams can work within the authorized-access zone, so no arming cycle starts if discipline holds
The Register ends the holding period in the coalition cantonment's proper secure storage
disadvantages: {FILE_COUNT} files over three nights on the vehicle ramp make a convoy pattern the cell can read by the second night
The chain of custody spreads across 60 to 80 containers and every hand that touches them
The trap stays armed behind you in an empty vault, leaving a booby-trapped room in your own compound for good
options.consequence: The archive goes down the mountain in crates while everyone watches everyone's hands. What arrives is what was carried, and proving nothing left the chain is the commission's first question and your answer forever.

costs.resource: chain-of-custody risk: 60-80 sealed containers, logged by two witnesses at both ends, every shift
costs.risk: a second-night ambush on the switchbacks, the cell's one clean shot at the whole Register in the open

decisionPoints.name: Reading Rights
decisionPoints.context: Sealed, the Register is a source of pressure. Opened, it becomes a weapon. Three parties have asked in writing for access, and refusing all three is itself a choice with a price.

options.title: Total Seal
advantages: The cleanest record for the commission: zero access, the strongest legal position
No faction can claim your detail took a side
The fourteen names on your roster stay unread with everything else, so your neutrality holds
disadvantages: The camp's pressure keeps building with no release, and crowd events grow weekly
The open-the-files faction works around you, so expect forged access orders and a sympathetic adept at a door
Sealed files answer no urgent question, so the cell's network stays hidden from coalition intelligence the whole time
options.consequence: The door stays shut and becomes the one thing every faction agrees on. Everyone who wanted the files looks for another way in, and every one of those ways runs through your perimeter.

costs.resource: crowd pressure keeps building: one escalation step per rumor cycle, with no release
costs.risk: a forged-order access attempt by your own side, which the charges cannot tell apart from a hostile one

options.title: Controlled Disclosure
advantages: Publishing the confirmed-coerced list of 1,400 names eases the camp's worst grief with proof on paper
It shows the Register's value publicly, hardening the will to protect it
The commission inherits a calmer Stair
disadvantages: The evidence is now tainted: the defense at every future trial starts with your partial release
Leaving a name off convicts it, because the camp assumes anyone not on the coerced list is guilty
Choosing names means reading files, and reading means readers, so the neutrality of not-looking ends by your own order
options.consequence: Fourteen hundred families get their answer early, and the Register is no longer sealed in any way that survives cross-examination. Mercy now, paid for in weaker verdicts later.

costs.resource: evidence integrity: the partial release is argued against at every trial the Register feeds for a decade
costs.risk: the names left off the list spark the exact vigilante violence the disclosure was meant to prevent

options.title: Admit the Precentor's Audit
advantages: The Precentor's reconciliationist team brings 20 trained adepts who strengthen compound security for the duration
The Order's senior survivor owes your detail a debt that will pay off in the long run
An audited inventory strengthens the manifest the commission signs
disadvantages: An audit is one faction's hand inside the drawers, dressed up as procedure
Whatever the team copies, and audit teams do copy, carries your co-signature into the Order's own war
The other faction sees you letting one side in as permission for both
options.consequence: Security improves and the inventory firms up, but the Register quietly enters ComStar politics through the door you opened. The commission gets everything except the certainty that it got everything.

costs.resource: political cost: your detail becomes a named creditor and debtor in the Order's factional accounts
costs.risk: audit copies surface later in a purge proceeding, traced back to your holding period

entries.event: Vault tamper alarm: the arming cycle starts. Everything else is now second priority.
Arming threshold. Get disarm authority onto the vault floor within 90 seconds, or the Register burns.
The remnant cell hits the vehicle ramp checkpoint, matching both earlier probes: the tamper attempt is the real effort, the ramp is a distraction.
The Stair camp surges up toward the compound gate; the alarms draw the crowd the way church bells draw a town.
The compound reaction force is fully committed across vault, ramp, and Stair. Anything more goes unanswered.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The commission lands in {COMMISSION_DAYS} days, and until its custody officer signs, every file is your responsibility. But the clock that really matters is short: 90 seconds from tamper to thermite. Hold those 90 seconds every time and the days take care of themselves. Lose them once and 11 worlds' worth of answers go up in smoke over {DISTRICT}.

opforSketch.composition: Word of Blake remnant cell: 12-20 effectives (Veteran), smallarms, breaching charges, 1-2 civilian vehicles, possibly one converted IndustrialMech held back in the city (UNCONFIRMED — basis: machine-shop power draws). Crowd events are a separate, unarmed pressure the generator should run on the Stair axis. Internal threats — forged orders, access irregularities — arrive through friendly channels.
opforSketch.behavior: The cell's objective is the vault's destruction, not the compound's capture; it will spend itself to start the arming cycle. Expect diversion at the ramp, main effort at the vault, and crowd surges timed to both. It treats the petitioners as a tool and the Order's factions as unwitting allies, and it is not entirely wrong about either.

forks.name: OPERATION NAMED NIGHT
forks.trigger: Register delivered complete; commission adjudication begins on schedule.
forks.consequence: The files map the stay-behind network across the district: 9 safe sites, 2 caches, a courier spine. The commission authorizes simultaneous strikes before the network learns what the Register held, and the unit that kept the files is asked to act on them.

forks.name: OPERATION UNWRITTEN
forks.trigger: The Register burns or leaves custody incomplete.
forks.consequence: The network the files would have named stays dark and goes active: sabotage tempo across the district within a month. The campaign to find by patrol and capture what could have been read from a drawer falls, with appropriate irony, to the detail that held the vault.

forks.name: OPERATION SPILLED INK
forks.trigger: A partial list — leaked, audited, or disclosed — circulates beyond control, traced to the holding period.
forks.consequence: Vigilante purges begin off an incomplete and partly wrong list in three district towns. The detail is retasked to protect accused collaborators from crowds armed with its own leaked paper.

storyElementSeed: In the vault doorway an acolyte reads the drawer labels without opening anything. He finds the drawer for his home district and stands in front of it a while, hands behind his back, then logs the cabinet temperature on his round sheet and walks on.

merc.situation.framing: The employer calls it an archive. The contract calls it a flammable building full of other people's secrets, and the chain-of-custody liability rider runs four pages, longer than the combat annex. Take the hint: on this job the enemy is anyone holding a match, a key, or a grudge, and the pay table only counts the first kind.

resourceGates.appliesTo: Carry It Out Under the Array
resourceGates.lackingText: With no unit lift, the convoy has to run the valley road 60 kilometers to the coalition cantonment instead of using the compound airfield. Three nights become six, the ambush risk doubles, and the cell gets four extra rumor cycles to learn the schedule.

skeleton: custodial force must keep an archive of informers intact and unread while its own order's factions, the network the files name, and a rigged self-destruct all contend for it ahead of an adjudication deadline
inspiration: the seizure and sealing of secret-police informer files, Berlin 1990

title: OPERATION COLD DOCKET
situation:
Liberation reached {DISTRICT} on {WORLD} in {YEAR}, and the occupation's records reached the Assize House eleven days later. The old bonded-customs hall now holds 214 detainees from the Protectorate's civil administration: the Director-General, his department heads, and the long line of dispatchers, registrars, and clerks who kept the machine running. The military governor's order is exact. All 214 must reach the tribunal alive, which sits in {TRIBUNAL_DAYS} days. Crowd deaths must be zero. And both counts will be audited. Your unit holds the building, the perimeter, and the tight gap between keeping those two numbers at zero.

Every night a crowd gathers in Weighbridge Square, up to {CROWD_PEAK} at the evening peak by police count. Five tram lines run into the square and feed it, and the square's shape funnels everyone toward the Assize House portico. The veterans' association, led by {NPC:resistance-leader}, has handed you a list of 31 names it wants turned over to 'people's custody,' and it reads the list aloud each night. The association buried 4,000 of its own during the occupation, so the list is more than talk.

Three things make the custody harder. First, the city still runs on its prisoners. The detainee in cell nine ran the water grid for eleven years, and the pumping schedule that keeps four districts supplied is partly in his head, so the public works office asks to consult him under escort every week. Second, counterintelligence flags 3 of the 214 as probable ROM cadre hiding behind collaborator cover, based on odd pay records and nothing firmer. The most dangerous men in the building are not the ones the crowd chants about, and moving them where anyone can see would warn whoever planted them. Third, a Word of Blake stay-behind cell wants the detainees dead before they can testify, because dead men name no networks. Two fires in the records annex in 16 days share the same incendiary residue, a solid forensic match. The cell's cleanest weapon is the crowd: a breach it starts, a fire that rides a crowd surge, a death the mob gets blamed for.

The hard ground comes in two parts. In front, the square funnels crowds onto your doorstep on tram schedules you do not control. Behind the building, the Bonded Basin offers an escape by water: two barges that can carry all 214 with escort. But the basin's lock gates are run from the Harbormaster's tower, 340 meters outside your perimeter, by a civilian crew that may simply not show up on the one night the barges matter. Ration tonnage, guard overtime, and lamp oil for the portico are all in annex B, and the governor's auditors have already questioned line 14.

objectives.primary: All 214 detainees alive and present on tribunal day, with zero crowd deaths blamed on the custody force.
objectives.secondary: Identify and quietly separate the 3 probable ROM cadre without any visible change in how detainees are handled.
objectives.bonus: Keep the weekly water-grid consultations going without a public incident, so the pumps keep running and the crowd never hears about the visits.

complications.name: The Square Funnels
complications.text: Five tram lines feed Weighbridge Square, and the square feeds the portico. The tram timetable sets the size of the crowd. Cutting tram service caps the crowd but starts a general strike within 72 hours, because the transit union buried its own during the occupation too.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Crowd event size scales with the tram service level. Cutting service halves the crowd peaks but, after 72 hours, starts a strike escalation track that adds unrest events across the city.

complications.name: The Lock Gates
complications.text: The barge escape needs 40 minutes of gate work by a civilian crew in a tower outside the wire. On a calm day that is one phone call. During a riot it is just a hope.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Barge evacuation needs the Harbormaster crew on station plus 40 minutes to cycle the gates. During any active crowd event, roll for crew availability. Putting troops in the tower beforehand makes evacuation reliable but is visible to everyone (see decision point).

complications.name: Cell Nine Runs the Pumps
complications.text: The water-grid director must consult weekly under escort, or four districts start losing water. Every consultation moves the building's most hated kind of prisoner, in daylight, on a set schedule.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Skip two consultations in a row and the district pumps start failing, a public-health clock that adds crowd grievance events. Each consultation you run is a movement the cell can watch and the crowd can find out about.

complications.name: Three Wrong Faces
complications.text: The probable cadre are mixed in among the clerks. Any visible move to separate them leaks through detainee trustees and guard-shift gossip within 24 to 48 hours, and warns the cell its men are suspected.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Changes to how detainees are handled leak on a 24-48 hour clock. If the cell learns its men are flagged, it escalates from arson-by-proxy to a direct breach attempt within one week.

decisionPoints.name: The Thirty-One
decisionPoints.context: The association reads its list aloud every night, and every night the angry silence after it gets shorter. The governor has left the response to the custody commander's discretion, in writing, and here 'discretion' is the polite Commonwealth word for liability.

options.title: Transfer the Thirty-One to Orbit
advantages: Removes the heart of the crowd's grievance: the nightly list has no one left to demand
The 31 top defendants become unreachable by mob, fire, or cell
The tribunal's headline cases are physically safe
disadvantages: The convoy has to cross the square or the basin, a flashpoint either way, and the crowd will know within hours
Tribunal counsel objects on the record: separating defendants from the evidence weakens 31 cases
The association calls the removal a rescue, and 'they are being taken beyond justice' becomes its next placard
options.consequence: The building's most dangerous prisoners are gone, and the crowd is left with anger and no target. History says it simply aims that anger at whoever remains.

costs.resource: one full company tied up in a single convoy, thinning the perimeter for 6 hours
costs.risk: the transfer convoy is the single most dangerous event of the whole custody period

options.title: Preliminary Hearings On-Site
advantages: Openness eases the pressure: 6 hearings a day, recorded, with gallery seats given to the association
The crowd's energy shifts from the portico to the courtroom
Early testimony locks in evidence before anyone can be intimidated
disadvantages: A published hearing schedule is also a published target schedule, giving the cell dates, times, and a gallery
Hearings create near-verdict moments daily, any of which can set off the square
Tribunal counsel is split: on-site hearings first may taint the main trial
options.consequence: The Assize House becomes a courthouse early, with a courthouse's calendar and a courthouse's crowds. The pressure comes off on a schedule, and so does the risk.

costs.resource: one platoon per hearing day committed to gallery and witness security
costs.risk: one gallery incident, real or staged, happening in front of recording gear and 200 witnesses

options.title: No Concessions, Harden the Line
advantages: The cleanest legal position: the tribunal gets an untouched case
No schedules, hearings, or convoys for the cell to plan around
The garrison's posture is simple to drill and easy to audit
disadvantages: With no release, the nightly crowds grow angrier, and crowd events escalate weekly
The governor's political standing drains at a steady rate, and the placards have started naming the governor
Hardening looks like protecting the accused, so recruitment for the association doubles
options.consequence: The line holds because it has to, every night, against odds that get worse every week. Clean law, rising risk, and the audit reads both columns.

costs.resource: political cost: the governor's standing drains weekly, and that standing is what shields the contract
costs.risk: when the breach finally comes, it comes at the peak of the anger curve instead of the middle

decisionPoints.name: The Tower
decisionPoints.context: The barge escape is the only exit that avoids the square. It all depends on a civilian-crewed tower 340 meters outside the wire, and the question is what to do about that before the night you actually need it.

options.title: Garrison the Tower Now
advantages: Evacuation becomes an order, not a hope: the gates cycle on your schedule
The tower overlooks the basin approach, a useful lookout against the cell's waterside moves
One less civilian dependency in the crisis plan
disadvantages: Openly occupying harbor infrastructure tells the crowd you have already decided the verdict
One platoon committed outside the wire, reachable only along the basin edge
The Harbormaster's office protests through the trade ministry, and annex B grows a line 15
options.consequence: You secure the exit and announce it in the same act. Now the crowd plans around the barges too, and the square's speakers have a new word: flight.

costs.resource: 1 platoon detached outside the perimeter for the whole custody period
costs.risk: the visible preparation speeds up the crowd's timeline, so the surge you prepared for arrives sooner because you prepared

options.title: Contract the Crew Quietly
advantages: Cheap, invisible, and deniable: a retainer plus a night-call bonus
No troops committed and no public signal
The crew knows the gates better than any platoon would
disadvantages: A paid crew can be paid by someone else, and the cell has money too
The crew lives in the city the crowd comes from, so on the worst night their loyalty competes with family at their door
You cannot make them come; if they do not, the plan is just a rumor with a receipt
options.consequence: The exit stays secret and stays soft. Whether it works at all gets tested the moment you actually need it.

costs.risk: one point of failure: four civilians showing up, and you cannot know if they will until the night the barges are the plan

options.title: Write Off the Barges
advantages: No dependence on civilians, towers, or lock machinery
You focus resources on the perimeter and the ground evacuation drill
At least armored night movement through the square is entirely under your command
disadvantages: The ground route crosses the crowd's home turf, so the funnel now works against you
You need 12 protected transports for 214 detainees, pulled from a garrison pool the auditors are already asking about
If the square is blocked on the night, there is no backup exit at all
options.consequence: The plan comes down to one door, and that door opens into Weighbridge Square. Everything now rides on the perimeter never failing, which is the very thing this plan was meant to guard against.

costs.resource: 12 protected transports from the garrison pool, held for an emergency that may never come
costs.risk: no backup: if the perimeter fails during a peak crowd, 214 lives are trapped behind one door and one mob

entries.event: Portico breach alarm: crowd pressure at the main doors pushes past the barrier line.
The shield line commits at the portico. From here on, 200 hand cameras record every contact.
Fresh crowds arrive by tram; the lines keep delivering on schedule no matter what they deliver into.
Fire risk peaks: the records-annex pattern shows the incendiary attempt rides the surge, not the front of it.
If the entry hall is not cleared, the custody floor is within reach. Twenty-five minutes is how long the building holds; after that the crowd decides.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Hold every breach under 25 minutes and every detainee to tribunal day, {TRIBUNAL_DAYS} days out. A detainee dead in your custody is a mob verdict signed with your name, and the audit, as the governor made clear, keeps that line forever.

opforSketch.composition: Primary pressure is the crowd: {CROWD_PEAK} at peak, unarmed, with an organized core around the veterans' association. The armed threat is a Word of Blake stay-behind cell, 8-15 effectives (Veteran), incendiary specialists with smallarms and breaching charges, operating under crowd cover; 0-1 light vehicles. Generator should keep direct fire engagements rare, brief, and catastrophic to the political situation when they occur.
opforSketch.behavior: The cell times action to crowd peaks and never engages the line directly: its victory is dead detainees by any hand, preferably the crowd's, ideally yours. The association's leadership wants custody transfers, not corpses — but it controls the crowd's grievance, not its hands, and knows it.

forks.name: OPERATION LONG GAVEL
forks.trigger: All 214 delivered to tribunal day; zero crowd fatalities.
forks.consequence: The tribunal sits for a projected 90 days, and everything that pressured the Assize House transfers to the courtroom: witnesses to protect, galleries to screen, and the 3 cadre cases — now formally charged — drawing the cell's last and best effort.

forks.name: OPERATION IRON CURFEW
forks.trigger: Detainee deaths in custody — by breach, fire, or engineered surge.
forks.consequence: The governor declares district martial law. The unit that lost the Assize House holds the curfew it caused: checkpoints, sweeps, and a city that has stopped distinguishing the custody force from the occupation it replaced.

forks.name: OPERATION MATCHHEAD
forks.trigger: Custody-force weapons kill civilians in the square, justified or not.
forks.consequence: An inquiry convenes with the unit as its subject. The only acquitting evidence is the cell itself: find the incendiary team, its residue-matched stocks, and its link to the breach nights — before the inquiry finishes finding you.

storyElementSeed: A guard walks the custody corridor handing supper trays through the slots. At cell nine he passes the tray without looking up; the man inside signed the water-rationing order that kept the guard's street alive two winters ago, and both of them know it, and the tray changes hands in silence.

merc.situation.framing: Before signing, read the indemnity schedule. It excludes 'civil disturbance outcomes,' which means every death in that square is billed to your account no matter whose hands did it. The employer bought a result, 214 alive and the crowd alive and the audit clean, and left you holding every event that produces a different number. Treat the discretion clause as the liability it is.

resourceGates.lackingText: With no unit lift, an orbital transfer has to wait for the governor's shuttle rotation, 11 days out. That fits inside the tribunal window only if nothing slips, so the option is locked with that timing shown.

skeleton: custody force must keep accused collaborators alive to a tribunal date against a crowd that wants them, a city that still runs on them, and a hidden cell that needs them dead before they testify

title: OPERATION MUSTER OUT
situation:
{WORLD} mostly freed itself. By the time coalition forces landed in {YEAR}, the Volunteers had already pushed the Protectorate garrison into two pockets, at a cost of three years of fighting. They are 2,600 fighters in 4 loose battalions organized by valley. They field 9 salvaged BattleMechs, 3 of them not currently working, plus 47 armed vehicles counting the converted farm equipment, and a field-phone network they built themselves that is faster than yours. Now the AFFS has taken back control, and it has handed you the kind of order nobody signs up to carry out: confine the Volunteers to cantonments and collect their weapons. In return you can offer amnesty certificates, veterans' pension cards, and 380 regular militia slots, for 2,600 applicants. Your unit runs the three cantonment sites on the Greenmantle bench and keeps the ledger. The ledger is the mission.

The lift schedule is fixed. Coalition transports leave in {LIFT_DAYS} days, carrying the heavy salvage and your unit onward. By standing order, anything not turned in or formally signed over by lift day minus 2 becomes contraband. But the order does not come with enough troops to seize contraband from 2,600 veterans of a war they won.

Three problems, worst one last. First, the 'Mechs. To the AFFS they are crown property recovered from a war zone. To the Volunteers they are back pay, proof of what they did, and the graves of the men who captured them. Both sides mean it. Second, paper. A forged document is going around on AFFS letterhead: a 'post-amnesty review' list of {LIST_NAMES} Volunteer names. The provost is confident it is fake, from the typeface and seal, but it looks real to people the Protectorate trained to fear lists, and turn-in attendance dropped by a fifth the week it appeared. The real question is who made it: a Word of Blake stay-behind trying to wreck the disarmament, or a Volunteer faction trying to wreck it for the opposite reason. Both theories fit every fact you have. Third, the arithmetic of resentment: 380 slots, 2,600 applicants, and every rejection letter goes to a man still deciding whether to hand in his rifle.

The hard ground is the incline. The three cantonments sit on the bench above the Greenmantle Escarpment. The only way down for anything over 20 tons is the cog-rail incline: one car, an 80-ton limit, and 40 minutes per round trip, run from a winch house at the top. Whoever holds the winch house decides whether the 'Mechs go down as turn-ins or stay up top as a standing threat. Right now a Volunteer honor guard holds it, under an unwritten agreement that both sides follow and neither side trusts.

objectives.primary: Finish the turn-in and cantonment processing of all 4 battalions by lift day minus 2, with no shot fired at any ceremony.
objectives.secondary: Trace the forged review list to its source, Blakist or Volunteer, with evidence that holds up to a provost review.
objectives.bonus: Fill the 380 militia slots with vetted Volunteers and hold the first muster parade before lift, with the signed-over lance, if any, on the parade.

complications.name: The Winch House
complications.text: Every heavy turn-in rides the incline, the incline is run from the winch house, and the winch house is held by an honor guard whose orders rest on a handshake. Taking it by force would prove the forgery right.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any plan that moves 'Mechs or heavy salvage needs the winch house crew's cooperation. Seizing it by force ends all ceremony attendance at once and starts the FAILURE fork's conditions. Negotiated access is a diplomatic action, resolved per event.

complications.name: Paper Against Paper
complications.text: The forged list cannot be un-printed. Your receipts, certificates, and pension cards are the answer to it, and they only work if every single one is honored every time.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each ceremony rolls for rumor strength. Left unanswered, attendance drops 15-30 percent per ceremony. Every honored certificate and settled grievance improves the roll; every clerical error worsens it.

complications.name: The Ledger Is the Weapon
complications.text: A lost receipt is not just paperwork. It is a man who handed over his rifle and cannot prove it. On this contract the clerks matter as much as the lances.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Ledger errors create grievance events. A site audit clears the built-up errors but costs that site a full processing day against the lift clock.

complications.name: Four Battalions, Four Tempers
complications.text: The valleys fought the same war but not in the same way. Any deal you make with one battalion, the other three demand to match before the ink dries.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The generator assigns postures: one battalion hardline, one cooperative, two watching. Any concession to one battalion forces a roll with the other three: match it, or take a grievance event.

decisionPoints.name: Nine Machines
decisionPoints.context: The 'Mechs are what disarmament really means here. Everything else is rifles and paperwork. These decide whether the war's winners get to keep what winning cost them.

options.title: Buy Them at Fair Salvage
advantages: A clean transfer of ownership: paid men sign receipts, and receipts end arguments
The price holds up in any audit, because the salvage rates are fair and posted openly
The hardline battalion's main grievance turns into cash its widows' fund can use
disadvantages: 1.6 to 2.2 million C-bills, from a budget sized for pension cards
The precedent spreads: every militia on every liberated world learns that holding 'Mechs through liberation pays off
The Volunteers who died taking the machines are now a line item, and their battalions will hear it put that way
options.consequence: Ownership transfers with no standoff, and the March learns the price of a salvaged 'Mech held by determined men. The bill comes twice: once now, once on the next world.

costs.risk: the precedent gets quoted on three liberated worlds within the year, a strategic cost your unit pays nothing for and the AFFS pays for a decade

options.title: Federate a Volunteer Lance
advantages: Four working 'Mechs stay with vetted Volunteer MechWarriors under AFFS commission, and five hulls turn in
It costs almost nothing in cash and puts the cooperative battalion's full weight behind the program
The federated lance at the first muster is the picture the whole policy needs
disadvantages: Vetting 4 MechWarriors in {LIFT_DAYS} days with the records the Protectorate left is really just guesswork
The lance cuts both ways: proof of loyalty if it holds, an armed precedent if it goes bad
The hardline battalion will demand the same deal for its 2 walkers within a week, so the matching problem is guaranteed
options.consequence: The Volunteers keep a fist and the AFFS keeps count of the fingers. Cheap and popular, but the vetting file is the thinnest paper in the plan.

costs.resource: political cost: you must defend the deal up the AFFS chain, where 'armed irregulars still under arms' reads worse than it does on the bench
costs.risk: one federated MechWarrior later tied to anything at all turns the picture into the indictment

options.title: Crown-Property Seizure on Schedule
advantages: By the book and free: the regulation exists, the order cites it, and the title was never in doubt
No precedent of payment or a federation deal for any future world to point to
The quartermaster's manifest closes with no exceptions
disadvantages: Ceremony attendance collapses the day the seizure notice goes up, which is exactly the proof the forgery promised
The winch house question goes live at once: the 'Mechs come down only if the honor guard allows it, and the notice tells them not to
Every likely outcome now runs through a confrontation at the top of the incline
options.consequence: The law is enforced at the one spot where the law has no troops. What happens next depends on which side blinks at the winch house, and the officer who wrote the order is 40 light-years away.

costs.resource: the cooperative battalion's goodwill, spent entirely on the day the notice goes up
costs.risk: an armed standoff at the winch house with 19 days on the lift clock and the forgery proven right in every way that counts

decisionPoints.name: The List
decisionPoints.context: The forged list works because it looks believable. Your counter-move has to prove it false faster than rumor can turn it into accepted fact.

options.title: Joint Commission of Inquiry
advantages: Provost and Volunteer investigators work side by side, and the openness itself is the message
Finds the source in 8-15 days if it can be found, with the search visible the whole way
Whichever theory proves out, the finding carries both signatures
disadvantages: Opening the records cuts both ways: people you have not vetted read your counterintelligence files
8-15 days is most of the lift clock, and the rumor works around the clock while the commission works office hours
If the source is a Volunteer faction, the finding becomes an accusation against the war's heroes, co-signed by their own
options.consequence: The joint inquiry becomes the relationship itself: shared files, shared findings, shared blame. It is slow and honest, and the answer it produces may be one nobody on the bench wants written down.

costs.resource: counterintelligence risk: your source-handling methods are visible to uncleared Volunteer investigators
costs.risk: the finding arrives after the ceremonies it was meant to save

options.title: Accelerate the Schedule
advantages: Squeeze 19 days of ceremonies into 9, and outrun the rumor with finished facts
Each completed ceremony is its own counter-evidence: certificates honored, nobody arrested
The lift clock gains a margin it does not currently have
disadvantages: Tired clerks make ledger errors, and ledger errors are exactly the grievance events the forgery feeds on
Faster ceremonies mean faster vetting at the militia-slot desk, so the 380 are chosen quicker and worse
The rush itself looks like fear, and the rumor adapts: 'they are hurrying it before the arrests'
options.consequence: Speed against story. If the clerks hold up, the program finishes before the fear does. If they slip, the program creates the very proof the forgery needed.

costs.resource: the ledger error rate triples during the rush, and each error is a grievance event waiting to happen
costs.risk: one bad ceremony at this pace does the damage of three at normal pace

options.title: The Governor Countersigns On Stage
advantages: The planetary governor personally countersigns amnesty certificates at every remaining ceremony, the strongest guarantee the AFFS can physically make
It answers the forgery head-on: the top authority's own hand against an anonymous list
In every comparable case the political officers can cite, attendance recovers within two ceremonies
disadvantages: The governor becomes both the program's single point of failure and its highest-value target at once
Guarding the governor takes a company per ceremony, pulled from the same force running the sites
If any countersigned Volunteer is later arrested for cause, and with 2,600 men there will be cause somewhere, the whole guarantee collapses after the fact
options.consequence: The state stakes its name on the bench. It works until it is tested, and the test, when it comes, aims at the one signature everyone was told to trust.

costs.resource: political cost: the governor's personal standing pledged against every future prosecution of a certified Volunteer
costs.risk: a provocateur incident at a ceremony now puts the governor at its center

entries.event: Shots or violence at a cantonment ceremony: the flashpoint, whoever caused it.
The honor guard at the winch house stands to and closes the incline. Heavy movement off the bench is now stopped.
Word reaches the other two cantonments by Volunteer field phone, which is faster than yours, so their version arrives first.
Battalion assemblies form at all three sites, armed with whatever has not been turned in yet.
It resolves or it does not: by 30 minutes either the ceremony ground is calm and the line re-forms, or the cantonment heads uphill into the bush with its weapons.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Lift day is fixed at {LIFT_DAYS} days. Everything not turned in by lift day minus 2 is contraband by standing order. But seizing contraband from 2,600 veterans of a war they won is not police work, it is the next war, and the order does not come with the force to fight it.

opforSketch.composition: No conventional OPFOR. The provocateur cell is 4-12 effectives — quality Veteran if Blakist stay-behind, Regular if Volunteer hardline faction; the ambiguity is the scenario. Worst-case engagement is infantry-scale violence at a ceremony with an armed crowd present and 1-2 Volunteer 'Mechs powering up. The Volunteers' 9 'Mechs and 47 vehicles are the theoretical force; the design intent is that they never deploy.
opforSketch.behavior: The provocateur seeks one massacre, witnessed and recorded. The Volunteers seek their pay, their pride, and proof the amnesty is real; nobody else wants to fight. Posture, ceremony discipline, and clerical accuracy are the effective weapons on both sides.

forks.name: OPERATION FIRST MUSTER
forks.trigger: All 4 battalions processed by lift day minus 2; no ceremony violence.
forks.consequence: The 380-slot militia stands up with the federated lance (if formed) at its core, and the unit is offered the training cadre contract: 90 days to make a militia out of veterans who already think they know — and partly do.

forks.name: OPERATION GREEN WINTER
forks.trigger: A cantonment empties into the bush armed, or the winch house standoff turns to force.
forks.consequence: Between 400 and 900 Volunteers go to the hills with their weapons and their grievance, led by men your ledger trained them to distrust. The counterinsurgency tasking that follows is written for the unit that was already on the ground.

forks.name: OPERATION BLACK ARMBAND
forks.trigger: A massacre or mass-casualty incident at a ceremony, whatever its authorship.
forks.consequence: Planet-wide unrest within 72 hours; the lift delays; the unit is confined to honor-guard and crowd-line duties under a board of inquiry while every valley holds funerals on the same day.

storyElementSeed: At a trestle table a clerk tags a rifle, reads its serial aloud, and hands across a receipt and a pension card. The militiaman reads the receipt twice, front and back. The line behind him watches what his face does before it decides anything.

merc.situation.framing: Strip away the ceremony language and the job is this: repossession agents for a government that wants both the gratitude and the guns. The contract's 'civil incident' clause makes your unit liable for outcomes you can influence but not control, which is the definition of every bad clause ever signed. Your one defense is the ledger: run it perfectly and it is armor, run it loosely and it is the plaintiff's exhibit A.

LIST_NAMES.unit: names on the forged review list

resourceGates.lackingText: Below 1.6 million, the buyout has to be paid in installments against next quarter's garrison subsidy. The Volunteers keep 4 'Mechs as collateral until the final payment, and the winch house agreement, honor guard and all, stays in place with them.

skeleton: garrison must convert a victorious irregular army into civilians on a fixed lift schedule, trading amnesty, pensions, and salvage claims for weapons, while a forged arrest list works to turn one ceremony into proof that disarmament is a trap
inspiration: partisan disarmament after liberation — Greece and Italy, 1944-45

title: OPERATION MIRROR BANNER
situation:
The Dragon's authority has not reached {WORLD} since the Protectorate took it in {YEAR}, but the Dragon's soldiers are still here. Your command keeps the resistance alive: three understrength lances scattered in the high country and 11 village cells across the Kiso Terraces. The occupier has chosen not to hunt you down. Instead, it has chosen to impersonate you.

Your intelligence calls the enemy formation UNIT MIRROR: an estimated {MIRROR_STRENGTH} ROM-trained troops operating 4 captured DCMS BattleMechs repainted in your colors, carrying your insignia, and answering challenges in passable local dialect. This is not a guess. An actuator serial number from a wrecked 'Mech matches one your side lost in the fighting at the spaceport, a solid match from 21 days ago. In 11 weeks, five atrocities have been done in your name: granaries burned at two terrace villages, a headman's family murdered, livestock seized at gunpoint 'for the resistance.' Recruitment has dropped 60 percent. Two cells have been lost in six weeks, both within days of being contacted by friendly couriers nobody actually sent. The pattern is clear: MIRROR approaches your people pretending to be fellow fighters, then captures them whole.

The deadline is a bureaucratic one, which makes it firm. The Protectorate governor has announced a reconciliation census in {CENSUS_DAYS} days. Every male aged 15 to 50 must register at a district station, where testimony booths record accounts of 'bandit crimes,' and ROM will mine those booths for intelligence. If the terraces still believe your side burned the granaries when census day comes, they will freely and accurately describe your real cells, at the booths, to the very enemy you exist to protect them from. The resistance survives the winter on what those booths record, or it does not.

The hard ground is the mountain passes. The Kiso Terraces stack six farming valleys against the mountains, and moving between them means traveling at night over the high passes, single file, in cloud. At night, in column, your troops and MIRROR's look identical, to a village watcher, to a sentry, and to each other. The problem of telling friend from foe has a hard physical limit, and that limit is a mountain in the dark. Your ISF liaison adds the obvious note: treat the courier network as compromised, and run trust audits. The note does not say where the time for those audits is supposed to come from. Honor demands you answer the atrocities. Survival demands you answer the census. These are two different jobs, and you have {CENSUS_DAYS} days for both.

objectives.primary: Set up a way to verify identity that ends cell losses to fake couriers within 30 days, without freezing recruitment.
objectives.secondary: Show the terrace villages hard proof, not just claims, that the occupier committed the atrocities, before census day.
objectives.bonus: Find UNIT MIRROR's base and pin its location down well enough to strike, with the fix good for at least 72 hours.

complications.name: Night Passes
complications.text: Every move between valleys risks running into a column that may be friendly, may be MIRROR, or may be a militia patrol, and you get 30 seconds to decide. Both wrong answers kill you: firing on friends now, or hesitating and getting ambushed.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Every move between valleys includes an identification encounter roll. A friendly-fire result feeds the enemy's narrative track; a hesitation result risks ambush. The verification method chosen at decision point one modifies this roll.

complications.name: The Courier Net Is the Wound
complications.text: Every verification scheme travels by courier, and couriers are exactly what MIRROR captures. Each captured courier weakens the scheme by a set amount, and you have to count that honestly.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Verification schemes age. Any scheme older than 20 days, or hit by a courier loss, drops one reliability step. Replacing a scheme costs 6 days of courier circulation, during which contact discipline is at its weakest.

complications.name: The Census Clock
complications.text: The booths record what the valleys believe. Every atrocity you leave unanswered adds testimony against the real Front, and every counter-fact you prove takes some away. What gets measured is belief, not truth.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Track a narrative score. On census day, that score sets the volume of denunciations, and cell-exposure events in the following campaign month scale directly with it.

complications.name: Your Own Colors
complications.text: Four enemy machines wear your insignia. Any fight near witnesses gets remembered by the valley as the Front fighting itself, or worse, the Front being wiped out by the Front, which is the story MIRROR wants.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Fighting MIRROR within sight of any village produces hostile-narrative events, unless the plan includes witness handling such as pre-briefed elders or recovered physical proof.

decisionPoints.name: Proof of Self
decisionPoints.context: The Front has to recognize its own people in the dark, fast, through farmers' hands. Any method strong enough to stop MIRROR is also a method MIRROR can use if it captures it.

options.title: Rotating Challenge Codes
advantages: Can be deployed in days over the existing courier net
Simple enough for village cells to use without training
A blown code costs one rotation, not the membership
disadvantages: The scheme rides the courier net, which is the very channel that is compromised
One captured courier with one current code table lets MIRROR pass as friendly for a full rotation
Code discipline across 11 cells of farmers is a hope, not a fact
options.consequence: Quick to deploy, but thin protection. The Front is safe only as long as its unluckiest courier stays uncaptured, one code rotation at a time.

costs.resource: courier net risk: distribution runs at double tempo every rotation cycle
costs.risk: a silent compromise, MIRROR holding a live code table and waiting, looks exactly like safety until it is used

options.title: Vouch-By-Acquaintance Network
advantages: Cannot be faked: contact only through faces known before the occupation
No code tables to capture and nothing to decrypt
Cell losses stop within days, because MIRROR cannot fake a shared childhood
disadvantages: Recruitment freezes: a man no member knows cannot join, so the 60 percent drop becomes the new ceiling
The network exists in people's heads, so every arrest now gives up more, because each member's contacts are the map
Operations between valleys slow to the pace of who knows whom
options.consequence: The Front becomes a closed circle: no impostor gets in, but no new recruit gets in either. It is safe this winter and smaller every winter after. And because each member's known contacts are the map, every capture costs more than one person.

costs.resource: recruitment: frozen at current strength for as long as this method runs
costs.risk: ROM interrogations pay off better, because every capture now maps a whole neighborhood of the network

options.title: Prove It By Action
advantages: Verify by joint operation: only the tasked cells know the task, so only real cells show up
It builds strength while it verifies, so the Front fights more, not less
MIRROR cannot get into position for operations it was never told about
disadvantages: Tempo rises, and so do ammunition use and exposure
Every joint operation is an opening MIRROR can take by arriving as the second cell, so the verification event is also the ambush site
Failed operations now carry a cost: an absent cell is treated as fake until proven captured
options.consequence: The Front proves itself by fighting, which is what it is for, but every proof happens in the open, where the enemy wearing your face is invited to show up.

costs.resource: operational tempo: ammunition and exposure spent on verification operations the campaign plan never called for
costs.risk: one ambushed joint operation kills two verified cells in a single night, the worst case of this method and the Front's worst night of the war

decisionPoints.name: Answering the Fires
decisionPoints.context: The actuator serial number, the paint samples, and three witness statements sit in a strongbox. Evidence proves nothing until the valleys have seen it, and every way of showing them costs something you cannot replace.

options.title: Broadcast the Evidence
advantages: The captured transmitter on the massif reaches every valley receiver at once
Serial numbers, salvage records, and witness statements read aloud, using the occupier's own logistics records against it
One broadcast resets the narrative score before the census, in a single night
disadvantages: ROM will locate the transmitter within 3 to 5 broadcasts, so it is gone within a week
A broadcast can be answered: expect a counter-broadcast naming your witnesses within days
The valleys hear it once, but MIRROR's fires they can see, and seeing sticks better than hearing
options.consequence: The Front spends its one broadcast asset loudly, all at once. What the valleys believe afterward comes down to whether proof read over a radio outweighs the burned granaries they can see and touch.

costs.resource: the massif transmitter: gone within 3-5 broadcasts, the Front's only broadcast asset lost for the war
costs.risk: the named witnesses need to be moved at once, three families through the passes in census season

options.title: Hunt UNIT MIRROR
advantages: Four 'Mechs need spare parts, and parts move on roads, so patient work can find their supply line
A battlefield is the one proof no counter-story survives: MIRROR dead in your colors, photographed, with ROM paybooks
Success delivers the bonus objective and the narrative at the same time
disadvantages: Your best lance and 2 cells drop all other tasking for 20 days or more
MIRROR is ROM-run, so its supply line may be set as bait, and the hunt may be walking into a trap
If census day arrives mid-hunt with nothing to show, the fires stand unanswered at the moment of testimony
options.consequence: Everything rides on producing the one thing that ends the argument: the impostors themselves, dead or unmasked, before the booths open. That bet is the whole campaign.

costs.resource: the Front's best lance and 2 cells committed; all interdiction tasking suspended for the duration
costs.risk: a baited supply trail costs you the lance, and with it the Front's power to mean anything the census could threaten

options.title: Standing Village Guards
advantages: The six most-threatened granaries get armed watches, so the next fire is fought, not just suffered
Protection is the proof the villages actually asked for, and presence beats broadcasts
Any MIRROR raid on a guarded village becomes the battlefield evidence the Front needs
disadvantages: Holding fixed positions is the one thing a guerrilla force cannot survive: static guards can be found, pinned, and destroyed
Six fixed postings tie up half the Front's infantry for as long as they last
MIRROR can just raid the seventh village; the guards protect points, but the story is everywhere
options.consequence: The Front plants its flag where the people are, which is honorable and visible, and exactly what every occupier's hunter-killer doctrine is written to punish.

costs.resource: half the Front's infantry tied to fixed postings; each guard-week is priced in exposure the generator tracks
costs.risk: ROM concentrates on one guarded village with militia armor support, and the guard post is trapped

entries.event: An unknown column challenges, or is challenged, at a night pass: the standing encounter your verification method has to answer.
The challenge-response window closes. Your options: commit, or break contact and pull back downslope. Wait past 30 seconds and the initiative goes to whichever column is lying.
If shots are fired, the pass is compromised, and a ROM watch covers it for the next 10 days.
Survivors' accounts reach the valley below by morning market. Whose story arrives first matters more than what actually happened.
On any confirmed contact, ROM sweeps the nearer valley: two days of house searches, and the cell there goes quiet or gets taken.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Census day is {CENSUS_DAYS} days out. On that day the valleys testify to what they believe, in booths your rifles cannot reach, and the Front survives the winter on what they say, or it does not. Every operation between now and then is also an argument before that census.

opforSketch.composition: UNIT MIRROR: {MIRROR_STRENGTH} ROM-trained effectives (Elite in covert work, Veteran in combat), 4 captured DCMS BattleMechs with authentic insignia and unit markings, light transport. On call behind them: Protectorate Militia sweep companies (Regular) and district ROM interrogation teams. Generator should make MIRROR rare, deliberate, and always ambiguous at first contact.
opforSketch.behavior: Impersonation-first doctrine: MIRROR engages civilians as theater and real cells as 'comrades,' taking them at the rendezvous, not in battle. It avoids any fight it cannot stage-manage and withdraws from honest contact. On exposure risk it pivots to discrediting the evidence — its survival condition is the valleys' uncertainty, not its own.

forks.name: OPERATION FIRST LIGHT
forks.trigger: MIRROR unmasked before census day — by battlefield proof or broadcast evidence that holds.
forks.consequence: The terraces turn: recruitment recovers in a month what it lost in a season, and the booths run dry. The Front's strength supports its first true offensive tasking — the district ROM fort that ran MIRROR, while its files on the program are still in one place.

forks.name: OPERATION LAST LANTERN
forks.trigger: Census day passes with the narrative unanswered; denunciation volume confirms cell exposure at scale.
forks.consequence: The network is burning by winter. What remains of the Front's leadership, files, and the three witness families must reach the coast pickup before the sweeps reach them — an extraction conducted by the hunted, through passes now watched by both kinds of enemy.

forks.name: OPERATION ASH ROOT
forks.trigger: The chosen authentication scheme is captured intact — MIRROR walks into the network as a verified friend.
forks.consequence: Three cells taken in nine days. The survivors rebuild from cutouts under a doctrine that trusts nothing it did not bury itself: the same war, restarted smaller, with the lattice's lesson paid for in full.

storyElementSeed: Two columns halt on opposite slopes of a night pass. A challenge lamp blinks twice. No answer comes. Both columns stand in the cold for eleven minutes, neither advancing, then back away down their own valleys, and the pass stays empty until morning.

merc.situation.framing: If the employer is the government-in-exile, learn the unwritten clause before the written ones. A hidden force that can be impersonated is a hidden force that can be tested, and the employer will be checking YOU at the same time you are checking everyone else. Expect tests. Pass them where they can see. The contract pays in scrip you can only cash after a liberation that is, for now, only a hope.

skeleton: resistance must keep recruiting while an occupier's impostor unit commits atrocities in its name, and every authentication measure strong enough to unmask the impostors also maps the resistance for the hunter

title: OPERATION COMMON TONGUE
situation:
The coalition is liberating {WORLD} with two armies that agree on the enemy and nothing else. Task Force NORTH is two DCMS battalions with aerospace attached. Task Force SOUTH is two AFFS battalions with an armor brigade. They are closing on the capital from opposite sides of the Verdigris Cut, and your unit holds the boundary between them under a boundary-force contract from the coalition field headquarters. Read the contract before you complain about the fighting: any boundary incident is docked from your pay at replacement cost, you get no salvage rights in either army's zone, and either House liaison can throw your sub-units out of his zone 'for cause,' with no appeal. The employer knows exactly what this job is. That is why it hired it out.

Here is the friction, one item at a time. Recognition codes: the DCMS will not share IFF codes with a force that carries AFFS liaison officers, and the AFFS will not drop its liaisons. So you run two separate radio systems plus a paper-and-flare recognition code, agreed over a tea kettle at the morning boundary meeting. Clocks: NORTH runs on local solar time, SOUTH on fleet standard, a 41-minute difference that has already dropped one artillery barrage on a grid square that was empty, but was only supposed to be empty 41 minutes later. Prisoners: Protectorate militia conscripts are surrendering in organized groups to SOUTH, whose prison camps have a bad reputation, while NORTH treats those same men as fighters fleeing the battle. The columns cross the boundary because rumor told them which camp to pick, and they cross right under DCMS guns to do it.

The defender understands all of this. The Word of Blake garrison, one understrength Level III plus militia, attacks along the boundary and retreats back across it. It also runs decoy transmitters that copy each army's radio signatures to trick them into firing across the boundary at each other. One decoy transmitter was recovered four days ago. The logic is simple: every allied shell that lands on an ally is worth a company to them.

The ground: the Verdigris Cut is a flooded open-pit mine trench, 14 kilometers long and 300 meters wide, with water 9 to 40 meters deep. It can only be crossed at three dragline causeways: ALPHA rated for 100 tons, BRAVO for 60, CHARLIE for foot troops and light vehicles only. The boundary between the two armies runs the full length of the Cut, so the causeways belong to nobody but you.
