H-hour for the joint assault on the capital is {HHOUR_DAYS} days away, and the order sets one written condition: 72 straight hours with no boundary incident, because the capital plan has the two armies fighting street by street, mixed together. Meanwhile the Blakists are demolishing the capital's three fusion plants, which engineers estimate will take {DEMOLITION_DAYS} days to finish. Every delay to H-hour is paid for in lost fusion plants.

objectives.primary: Deliver 72 hours in a row with no boundary incident, so H-hour confirms on schedule.
objectives.secondary: Find and destroy the decoy-transmitter teams working along the Cut.
objectives.bonus: A written procedure for surrendered-personnel crossings, agreed and signed by both contingent headquarters.

complications.name: Two Clocks
complications.text: The two contingents' clocks are 41 minutes apart, and neither will switch. Every joint action that crosses the boundary either goes through your command post to be converted both ways, or it goes wrong on the 41-minute gap.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any cross-boundary fire mission, movement order, or deconfliction request rolls for a time-base error unless your CP converts it both ways first. A conversion failure produces the empty-grid barrage event, or a not-empty-grid one.

complications.name: Red Cards
complications.text: Each liaison can throw your sub-units out of his zone for cause, and 'cause' is whatever he decides at the morning meeting. The more friction there is, the smaller your usable force gets.
complications.mechanicalEffect: After any incident in a zone, that House's liaison may red-card the sub-unit involved: it is barred from that zone for 96 hours, and you must rebuild the boundary coverage plan around the gap.

complications.name: The Causeway Ratings
complications.text: ALPHA carries 'Mechs, BRAVO carries mediums and lighter, CHARLIE carries men. The defender knows the weight limits as well as you do and ends every raid at a crossing your heavy units cannot follow across.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The causeway weight limits constrain any pursuit across the Cut, and the defender always withdraws by a crossing that fits its own weight class. Demolishing any causeway permanently reroutes both enemy and friendly heavy traffic through the ones that remain.

complications.name: Decoy Transmitters
complications.text: Near the boundary, treat every sensor contact as friendly until proven hostile, which is the opposite of what any crew is trained to do. The recovered transmitter copied a DCMS lance command frequency almost exactly.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Contacts near the boundary that show up on sensors alone are unreliable. Engaging without visual or a second source risks firing on your own side. Requiring confirmation adds 2-4 minutes to every response, and that is the gap the enemy raids through.

decisionPoints.name: Three Causeways
decisionPoints.context: The causeways are the only links across the boundary. How you hold them decides what kind of war happens along 14 kilometers of water.

options.title: Garrison All Three
advantages: A presence at every crossing: nothing moves over the Cut unseen
Both liaisons get what they asked for, so the red-card pressure drops
Surrendered columns meet a checkpoint instead of a no-man's-land
disadvantages: Three fixed positions, each too thin to stop a deliberate raid
The Level III can mass against any one garrison and outnumber it locally on a night of its choosing
Your reserve shrinks to a single lance
options.consequence: Coverage everywhere, strength nowhere. The boundary is well-managed but thinly defended, and on any given night the enemy chooses which of those two facts matters most.

costs.resource: reserve cut to one lance for the whole contract
costs.risk: beaten piece by piece: one garrison overrun before the reserve can cross 7 kilometers of boundary road

options.title: Hold ALPHA, Drop BRAVO and CHARLIE
advantages: Concentrate your strength: one crossing, fully defended, with the reserve behind it
The defender's hit-and-run-across doctrine loses two of its three exits
You replace hopeful patrolling with a sure block along 14 kilometers
disadvantages: A post-war bill: the provisional government needs those causeways, and blowing them lands politically on whoever ordered it
Surrendered columns and civilian traffic all funnel through ALPHA into your checkpoint line, with all the problems crowds bring
Funneling everything through ALPHA also funnels it for the enemy, so ALPHA becomes the one place every problem on the boundary shows up
options.consequence: The boundary simplifies to one gate, strongly held and owned by you, along with every line, claim, and grievance that now has only one place to go.

costs.resource: political cost: two causeways charged against the coalition's rebuilding budget, with your unit's name on the demolition order
costs.risk: a mass surrender and a Blakist raid arriving at ALPHA in the same hour, with the crowd in the kill zone

options.title: Mobile Patrol with Joint Liaison Teams
advantages: Flexible: the patrol goes wherever the last incident was not
The only working code-sharing setup on the planet, one DCMS and one AFFS officer in the same vehicle, deconflicting in real time
No fixed target for the decoy teams to plan against, so they have to guess
disadvantages: The gaps are built in: 14 kilometers, only so many patrols, and the enemy can count
The two liaison officers are a single point of failure, and one ambush kills the deconfliction setup and both contingents' trust at once
The patrol pace wears out machines faster than the contract's maintenance budget covers
options.consequence: The boundary is held by movement and by two officers' working relationship. It works until the night the enemy targets that relationship itself, which a captured map case suggests they have thought about.

costs.resource: maintenance: patrol pace at 160 percent of the contract's budgeted rate
costs.risk: the joint liaison vehicle is the highest-value target on the boundary, and both Houses' codes ride in it

decisionPoints.name: The Columns
decisionPoints.context: Surrendered militia columns keep crossing the boundary toward SOUTH's camps, under NORTH's guns, through your ground. The contract says nothing about this. The guns do not.

options.title: Escort the Crossings
advantages: Order at the boundary: set crossing times, with your vehicles flanking the columns
Casualties drop right away, since no escorted column has ever been fired on in any case on file
SOUTH's liaison becomes your ally in every dispute
disadvantages: Your escorts stand between DCMS weapons and what the DCMS considers lawful targets
NORTH's liaison logs every escort as meddling in its zone, and the red-card count climbs
Each escort is a boundary incident waiting on one nervous gunner from either side
options.consequence: You protect the crossings by putting your own machines physically between the two sides. The columns survive and the contract's record fills up, and now the 72-hour clean streak depends on every single escort going perfectly.

costs.resource: escort duty: one lance per crossing window, off boundary patrol
costs.risk: one shot during an escort is an incident with your unit physically in the middle of it, exactly the case the deduction clause was written for

options.title: Turn the Columns Back
advantages: Boundary incidents stop being your problem, because the crossings end
NORTH's liaison endorses the policy in writing the same day
The boundary force goes back to watching the boundary instead of managing a migration
disadvantages: The columns go back to the very custody they crossed a kill zone to escape
What happens to them there is recorded elsewhere, and you will read about it for years
SOUTH's liaison files a protest with the coalition headquarters that hired you, and the employer's own conscience clause stirs
options.consequence: The boundary quiets down and the contract's record stays clean, paid for with something the contract never priced. The mercenary trade has a long memory for units that learned to stop counting that cost.

costs.resource: reputation: the policy follows the unit into every future contract talk where the other side has heard about it
costs.risk: a turned-back column forces the crossing anyway, at night and unescorted, so the incident happens regardless, and bigger

options.title: Broker a Formal Corridor
advantages: A signed crossing procedure turns the boundary's worst flashpoint into a schedule
Both House signatures on one document, which achieves the bonus objective as a side effect
It lasts: the corridor outlives the operation and the contract
disadvantages: Days of staff work at two headquarters that share no building, no code, and no clock
While it is unsigned, the columns keep coming and the other two options keep happening anyway
Either House can kill it with one staffing delay, and neither pays a price if it dies
options.consequence: The long game: a procedure instead of more armor. If it signs, the boundary goes quiet, which is the contract fulfilled. Until it signs, every day is the same day, plus negotiation.

costs.resource: your executive officer and both liaison officers tied up shuttling between staffs for the whole negotiation
costs.risk: the corridor gets signed the day after the incident that would have justified it

entries.event: Cross-boundary fire alarm: weapons are landing across the boundary, and at first neither the source nor the target is confirmed.
The nearest patrol moves to get between the two sides. That is the contract's method, and the contract's most dangerous minute.
Both liaison channels demand the same facts in different formats on different clocks. Your CP's double conversion is now the only version both sides accept.
If it drags on, local commanders on each side start 'protective' repositioning that the other side reads as getting ready to attack.
Either one agreed timeline of the incident reaches both headquarters, or two different timelines exist and the 72-hour clock resets to zero.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: H-hour confirms only after 72 hours in a row with no incident, and H-hour is {HHOUR_DAYS} days out. Every reset costs fusion plants downstream: the demolition finishes in {DEMOLITION_DAYS} days and will not wait. Whether the capital still has power after liberation is the difference between a contract fulfilled and a contract merely survived.

opforSketch.composition: Word of Blake garrison remnant: one understrength Level III committing 6-12 units (Veteran) to seam operations at any one time, 2-3 false-emission decoy teams (Elite, vehicle-mounted), Protectorate Militia screening elements (Green). Generator should present the Level III as raid packages, never a massed defense.
opforSketch.behavior: Raids exclusively along and through the boundary; withdraws across causeways its own weight class can use and pursuit cannot. Decoy teams bait cross-seam fire by imitating each contingent's signatures. The defender's victory metric is allied incidents per week, not ground held — it is fighting your contract, not your lances.

forks.name: OPERATION JOINED HANDS
forks.trigger: 72 clean hours delivered; H-hour confirms.
forks.consequence: The joint capital assault proceeds with both contingents interleaved block by block — and the boundary force, having kept the seam, is assigned the seam's continuation: the assault corridor where NORTH's and SOUTH's blocks meet, all the way to the plant district.

forks.name: OPERATION SANDBAG
forks.trigger: The 72-hour clock resets past the demolition estimate; H-hour slips indefinitely.
forks.consequence: The plants are lost and the assault is repriced into a siege. The unit digs in along the Cut for a winter rotation the contract never priced, holding a boundary that now divides three armies that all consider the campaign someone else's failure.

forks.name: OPERATION REAR RANK
forks.trigger: Unit weapons kill allied personnel — decoy-baited or not.
forks.consequence: Both liaisons red-card simultaneously: the unit is pulled to rear-area security at the coalition logistics hub while a board of inquiry sits on the incident. The contract's deduction clause executes; the rear area, naturally, turns out not to be quiet.

storyElementSeed: At the causeway midpoint, two liaison officers who do not share a language take tea from the same kettle at 0600 and check each other's incident logs line by line, pointing at numbers. When the figures match, each initials the other's page, and the day is allowed to begin.

is-kurita.situation.framing: Task Force NORTH's order is not cruelty; it is the law as the district reads it. A Protectorate soldier who runs from custody is running from judgment, and to put off judgment is to put off duty. Yes, the Davion camps are softer, and that softness is why the columns walk west. The boundary force is asked to help neither the flight nor the pursuit, only to keep the boundary itself from becoming the battlefield. This order is exact. Follow it exactly.

resourceGates.appliesTo: Hold ALPHA, Drop BRAVO and CHARLIE
resourceGates.lackingText: With no depot access, you have no demolition stores of your own, so you must beg the charges from Task Force SOUTH's engineers. The favor is paid in salvage: the option's C-bill cost converts to a salvage-rights claim on your next recovery.

skeleton: boundary force must keep two allied contingents that share neither codes, clocks, nor custody doctrine from fighting each other across a seam the defender deliberately attacks, with every incident billed to the force holding the line and a confirmation clock that resets on each one
inspiration: coalition boundary friction at Kasserine Pass, 1943

title: OPERATION QUIET CLOISTER
situation:
The employer's official paperwork calls this public-health quarantine enforcement. The operational annex, which far fewer people see, describes the real job: destroying the Communion of the Five Pillars, a Word of Blake-aligned enclave holding a walled arcology-monastery in the Cistern Vale on {WORLD}, {YEAR}. The population is 800 to 1,400, of whom 200 to 280 are armed: one Level II equivalent of BattleMechs and armor plus militia infantry in prepared wall positions. The last parish census, four years old, counted 240 children inside. Treat every figure as rough, because the Communion stopped reporting to anyone once it stopped needing anyone.

Two clocks govern this, and neither is yours. The first is inside the wall. A defected deacon's diagram shows the compound's fusion plant with its safety systems deliberately disabled, which means the congregation can start a reactor meltdown 40 to 70 minutes after they decide to, killing everything within 1.2 to 2.1 kilometers plus a fallout plume. The diagram is 23 days old and low confidence, and the Maskirovka annex says only, in a carefully hedged sentence, that it neither believes nor disbelieves it. The second clock is in the sky. Analysis of the Blakist resupply flotilla that serves hidden enclaves predicts its next arrival window in {FLOTILLA_DAYS} days. If it arrives while your cordon is still up, the besiegers become the trapped, and the vale has only one road out.

The ground is karst limestone. The compound draws its water from cave galleries under the vale. Three mapped cave mouths open outside the wall, and the galleries connecting them are unmapped past the 400-meter survey line. There is no radio underground, so parties below ground are out of contact for 20 to 90 minutes at a stretch. The Communion has held this vale for two generations and knows its own caves.

Then there are the people leaving. Since the cordon closed, the Communion has been releasing its people in batches: 60 elderly on day two, 41 on day five, each batch walking to the wire under white cloth. Screening at the relief camp 6 kilometers back has already caught 2 people with false identities in the first batch, so cadre are almost certainly being slipped in among them. But the leavers are also genuinely old and genuinely sick, and each batch uses up escort, decontamination, and registration capacity the camp cannot spare. Refuse a batch and you hand the Communion propaganda for the week. Accept a batch and you accept whatever is hidden inside it. The Maskirovka observer at your headquarters files a report every day, watches which choice you make each time, and has offered no opinion so far, which everyone present correctly reads as its own kind of pressure.

objectives.primary: Destroy the enclave's ability to fight while keeping the reactor cold, with no meltdown before or during the assault.
objectives.secondary: Get the non-combatant population out alive and screened, and let no more false identities through after the first batch.
objectives.bonus: Capture the Communion's signals room intact, because its traffic logs lead to the other hidden enclaves the flotilla serves.

complications.name: The Plant
complications.text: Once started, the meltdown takes 40 to 70 minutes, according to a low-confidence diagram. The safeties were disabled by people who pray in the plant hall. Knowing the timing is not the same as knowing what the congregation will do.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Any assault alarm rolls for whether the meltdown starts. Once it starts, a hidden 40-70 minute clock runs, ended only by seizing the plant hall or an engineer performing an emergency shutdown. The generator may secretly vary the clock within, or slightly beyond, that range, because the diagram is low confidence and the table should feel that.

complications.name: The Galleries
complications.text: The caves are a way in, a way out, and a blindfold all at once. Parties underground have no radio and cannot be recalled, and the Communion's counter-tunnel watch has had two generations to prepare the ground.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Underground elements are out of command for 20-90 minutes per leg: no recall, no updates, and they follow the orders they were given. Past the 400-meter survey line, they move at half speed and are exposed to ambush until they map the way by moving through it.

complications.name: The Leaver Batches
complications.text: Every batch is both mercy and infiltration in one line. The camp's screening line is the second front, and it is run by medics.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each batch uses one day of the camp's screening and escort capacity. Refusing a batch costs you narrative and morale and raises the meltdown risk. Accepting one rolls for cadre slipping through, and any who get through report your cordon positions back inside, accurate to within 24 hours.

complications.name: The Observer
complications.text: The Maskirovka files a report every day. Certain words must never appear in your logs, and certain orders come only by word of mouth, so that everything can be denied later. Whatever you decide here will be quoted afterward, with or without its context.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each decision-point choice adds to a political record the campaign layer reads after the mission. Compensation claims, commendations, and the employer's next contract terms all draw on the observer's file.

decisionPoints.name: Three Doors
decisionPoints.context: You can empty the enclave by talking, empty it by cutting off water, or take it by force. Each path kills a different number of people, and none of those numbers can be known ahead of time.

options.title: The Deacon Channel
advantages: {NPC:intel-source} still has standing inside, so staged-surrender terms can reach the moderate congregation under the inner circle
Every family that walks out reduces what every later option has to deal with
Talking costs no ammunition and builds the screening camp's records
disadvantages: Days spent under the flotilla clock, which does not pause for negotiations
His safe-conducts deliver exactly the people the inner circle is willing to lose, so watch what each success tells you about who remains
If talks collapse in public, the inner circle gets its siege story at peak attendance
options.consequence: The patient path. The enclave empties from the outside in: the moderate families leave, the hard core stays, and the calendar burns down while you buy people out one batch at a time, until either the flotilla arrives or the inner circle ends the deal.

costs.resource: flotilla margin: 6-9 days of the {FLOTILLA_DAYS}-day window spent talking
costs.risk: each negotiated exit leaves behind a harder, more fanatic core for the final assault to take

options.title: Cut the Water
advantages: Damming the three cave mouths leaves the compound's cisterns with {CISTERN_DAYS} days of water, and thirst empties wall positions faster than fire would
No assault casualties while it works, and the engineering is straightforward
Batches of leavers speed up as the cisterns run low, so the population separates itself from the garrison
disadvantages: It is a collective punishment against a population that is mostly ordinary congregation, and it earns the observer's longest file entry
The surge of leavers triples the screening load at a camp already short, and the cadre's best traffic rides that worst crowding
The inner circle controls the story inside the wall: 'the unrighteous have closed the springs' is a sermon aimed straight at the plant hall
options.consequence: The siege becomes a matter of water. It works on a known schedule, and every day of it is preached inside as prophecy, while the meltdown risk climbs as the cistern gauge falls. The generator ties the two together.

costs.resource: camp screening: the number of leavers triples for the duration, and cadre-passage rolls worsen to match
costs.risk: the device answers the thirst: the meltdown risk rises each day the cisterns drop below half

options.title: The Galleries Assault
advantages: Engineer-led teams go underground to the plant hall while a wall assault is timed to match, the only option that can take the reactor before any clock matters
If it works inside the week, speed closes off the flotilla problem entirely
Seize the plant hall and every other problem shrinks to a cordon and a screening line
disadvantages: Everything rides on the low-confidence diagram and the unmapped 400 meters
Underground teams have no radio and cannot be recalled, so if the situation changes mid-assault, the plan runs anyway, as written, in the dark
Two attacks at once, above and below ground, on separate clocks with no link between them, so the ways it can fail multiply rather than add
options.consequence: The fast door, opened blind. If the diagram is honest and the caves are passable, it ends in an afternoon. Each 'if' is paid for by the people sent beyond recall to test it.

costs.resource: engineer teams sent beyond recall, out of contact for the whole assault
costs.risk: the diagram is wrong by one corridor, and the plant-hall team arrives at minute 50 of a 40-minute clock

decisionPoints.name: The Second Clock
decisionPoints.context: The flotilla window opens in {FLOTILLA_DAYS} days. The mouth of the vale is the only ground a relief landing can use, and the question is what the cordon can spare to hold it.

options.title: Fortify the Vale Mouth Now
advantages: A third of your force dug in on the only usable landing zone, so if the flotilla comes, it lands into prepared ground
The work is visible from the wall, so hope inside fades with every earthwork
The cordon's rear is now secured, not just assumed safe
disadvantages: The cordon itself thins by a third for the whole period, and the enclave's wall patrols will map the thin spot within days
If the flotilla does not come, you lengthened the siege for nothing
The engineering work competes with everything the other options need
options.consequence: Insurance bought at the cordon's expense. The enclave watches you prepare for a landing that may never come, while the gap your preparation opened is now watched by people praying for exactly that landing.

costs.resource: cordon strength: a third of your force fixed at the vale mouth for the duration
costs.risk: the enclave reads the thinned sector right and runs a breakout, or a supply column, through it

options.title: Keep the Cordon Whole
advantages: The siege runs at full strength, and every door option runs at its best speed
No gap for the wall patrols to find
The flotilla window is, after all, only a medium-confidence estimate
disadvantages: If the flotilla arrives, your force is caught between the wall and the landing zone with neither prepared
The annex calls this 'acceptable concentration risk,' but the annex does not stand in the vale
Pulling back under a relief landing means abandoning the siege works and the screening camp's security in the same hour
options.consequence: Full pressure now, full exposure later. The bet is that the siege ends before the sky opens, and the only thing backing that bet is a medium-confidence estimate with nothing of its own at stake.

costs.risk: the two-front hour: the flotilla lands at the vale mouth while the wall sallies, and the cordon fights both directions at once or fights neither

options.title: Request Coalition Aerospace
advantages: A coalition fighter wing on call makes the flotilla's approach a fight, the strongest deterrent you can get
No ground force pulled away, so the cordon and the door options continue untouched
The threat alone may close the window without a shot
disadvantages: It spends the favors the employer is owed, so the employer will owe you proportionally less afterward
The wing can only stay 10 days, which starts a third clock you must guess against the second
The observer's file notes who invited foreign fighters over a Capellan vale, in those exact words
options.consequence: The sky problem is solved with borrowed strength and borrowed standing. If the window and the 10 days overlap, it was good statecraft. If they miss, the favor is gone, the file is written, and the flotilla still sails.

costs.resource: political cost: a coalition-scale favor drawn on the employer's account, repaid out of your unit's standing
costs.risk: the 10-day window on the wing misses the flotilla window, spending both clocks with no coverage when it matters

entries.event: A reactor heat spike is detected, the sign of a meltdown starting, or an assault alarm sounds, whichever comes first.
Plant-hall seizure teams go in if they are in position. If not, the withdrawal order goes out: everyone beyond 2.5 kilometers.
Cordon posts inside 1.5 kilometers pull back or dig in. The leaver gate closes, and whoever is in the screening lane stays there.
Earliest the meltdown could hit. From now until T+70:00, nothing moves toward the wall for any reason.
Latest the meltdown could hit. If the vale is still standing, either the diagram overestimated the timing, the seizure worked, or the meltdown was a bluff, and only the plant hall knows which.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: From heat spike to meltdown is 40 to 70 minutes, on a low-confidence diagram. Either you hold the plant hall within 40 minutes, or everyone you command stands beyond 2.5 kilometers and finds out what the diagram was worth. And the flotilla window opens in {FLOTILLA_DAYS} days no matter what, so the siege ends, one way or another, before the sky becomes a second front.

opforSketch.composition: Communion forces: one Level II equivalent of mixed BattleMechs and armor (Regular skill, fanatic morale — does not rout, does not surrender as units), 200-280 militia infantry on prepared wall positions, and a ROM cadre of 10-20 (Elite) running internal security, the plant hall, and the leaver-seeding program. Generator should weight the defense toward infantry and fortification; the Level II is the counterattack reserve, not the line.
opforSketch.behavior: Defensive theology: the Communion fights at its wall and husbands the device as the final sermon. No sallies unless the flotilla lands. The ROM cadre is the rational actor inside — it runs the leavers, reads the cordon, and will trigger nothing while its own exit remains plausible. The inner circle is the irrational actor, and the two are not always in agreement; the generator may play the seam.

forks.name: OPERATION DRY SLIP
forks.trigger: Enclave reduced, reactor cold, signals annex taken intact.
forks.consequence: The traffic logs map the flotilla's circuit: four enclaves, two landfall patterns, one predictable bunkering stop. The employer wants the bunkering stop ambushed during the very window the siege just beat — the intelligence is freshest exactly while the unit is most spent.

forks.name: OPERATION GREY RAIN
forks.trigger: Excursion — by initiation, assault accident, or the model being wrong.
forks.consequence: The vale is a plume map and the camp of 1,200 becomes a camp of 9,000 as the downwind valleys empty. The reduction tasking converts to relief operations under contamination protocols, run by the force that watched it happen from 2.5 kilometers.

forks.name: OPERATION STRANGER'S BREAD
forks.trigger: Cadre passage through the leaver screening is confirmed after the fact.
forks.consequence: Between 4 and 11 ROM cadre hold camp registrations and ration cards. The camp's security becomes a counter-infiltration tasking conducted among genuine refugees — every measure that might find them is a measure applied to people who have already lost everything once.

storyElementSeed: At the wire an elderly leaver unwraps a cloth bundle for inspection: seed packets, a photograph, a brass cup. The soldier inventories the items on a form with four carbon copies, hands three back, and waves the next one forward. The queue moves at the speed of the form.

merc.situation.framing: The contract says quarantine enforcement; the indemnity annex says reactor. The annex is the part that matters. Note clause 31: 'outcomes attributable to deliberate energy release by the quarantined population' are excluded from employer liability, which means that if the device fires, it is officially nobody's fault and in practice yours. Price the galleries accordingly.

FLOTILLA_DAYS.unit: days until the predicted flotilla window

CISTERN_DAYS.unit: days of compound water if the cave mouths are dammed

resourceGates.lackingText: Without depot engineering stocks such as shoring, breaching kits, and hardline comm spools, the underground teams are out of contact the whole time instead of only in stretches. Their time out of command doubles, and the two attacks must be timed blind.

skeleton: siege force must end a fortified congregation's resistance with its rigged reactor cold while a predicted relief flotilla prices every day of patience and every batch of released believers both relieves and infiltrates the cordon

title: OPERATION FIVE HEARTHS
situation:
Someone is raiding three systems' worth of coalition logistics from a hidden base, and the employer has narrowed it to one continent. Your contract is to narrow it to a single grid square. Read the fee structure before you celebrate the retainer: 40 percent on signing, and the other 60 percent only on two-source confirmation of the site's exact location. The strike package, allied aerospace plus a ground battalion, commits exactly once. A false hit sends it against nothing, the raiders relocate, and the contract is voided with a blacklist and damages. The employer has been burned twice on this hunt already, which is why the terms read like a grudge.

The target is a Word of Blake hidden operating base on {WORLD}'s outback continent, empty except for grazing leases, bore-well fields, and survey stations. Analysis gives five possible sites, HEARTH ONE through FIVE, spread across 60,000 square kilometers: two flagged by heat readings, three by diverted grain and fuel shipments. The base has relocated twice in 14 months, each time within 72 hours of a change in coalition overflight patterns, going by the age of the refit debris at both abandoned sites. Working assumption: they have a trip-wire that detects reconnaissance and a rehearsed drill to relocate within 72 hours of it going off. Anything loud enough to confirm the base is loud enough to make them move it.

Your cover is a contracted mineral survey, and the cover has to actually work: real instruments and real assay filings lodged with the lease registry on a real schedule. The registry is public, so the enemy can read it too, which means a survey that stops surveying is a flare with paperwork attached.

The ground is the Chalk Maze: eroded pale badlands where ground radar throws false returns off the chalk and a vehicle track crumbles away into the whiteness within a day of wind. The key to the whole analysis is water. Nine working bore-wells serve the entire region, all metered for the grazing leases, and a garrison of 200-plus people has to drink somewhere. Buried in that slow, dull bore-well data is a water-draw pattern that matches no livestock herd. The last limit is the sky: the dust season shuts down all optical and sensor work in {STORM_DAYS} days. After that, the base winters where you cannot find it, and the spring raids, one every {RAID_INTERVAL} days on the recent pattern, are as good as already paid for while your invoice sits unpaid.

objectives.primary: Deliver two-source confirmation of the base's exact location before the dust season shuts down collection.
objectives.secondary: Keep the survey cover intact to the end of the contract, because the cover company is real, registered, and meant to be reused.
objectives.bonus: A pattern-of-life package, covering garrison strength, lift schedule, and watch rotations, good enough for the strike package to plan against.

complications.name: The Tripwire
complications.text: Burned twice already, the site treats any suspicion as confirmation. Its relocation drill is rehearsed, you do not know what sets it off, and the only sure thing is the 72 hours.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each active measure, such as an overflight deviation, a close approach, bore tampering, or planting a sensor in watched ground, rolls against detection. On a suspicion result, a hidden 72-hour relocation clock starts, and only action inside it can matter.

complications.name: The Cover Must Work
complications.text: The survey is a real company, not a costume. Assay filings are due at the registry on schedule, and skipped filings stand out in any audit, including the enemy's.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Survey teams must produce real filings on a fixed calendar. Each crisis week that pulls teams off survey work risks a registry flag, and two flags blow the cover and start the COMPROMISED fork's conditions.

complications.name: Chalk Ghosts
complications.text: The Maze swallows signals. Radar ghosts, magnetometer noise, tracks gone by morning: on 40 percent of the candidate ground, the data is unreliable and you have to judge what to trust and what to throw out.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Sensor results across 40 percent of the Maze include false contacts. Each false contact you accept into the analysis weakens your confirmation, and each one you investigate costs 2-3 days of team time.

complications.name: The Raids Continue
complications.text: Every {RAID_INTERVAL} days, another strike lands somewhere in three systems, and another message arrives asking how the survey is going. The employer's patience runs out a little more each time.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Each raid during the contract advances a contract-relations track. At the third raid, the employer demands an interim assessment. At the fifth, the fee is renegotiated downward.

decisionPoints.name: How Loud to Look
decisionPoints.context: How hard you collect is the whole game: extra effort buys speed but spends concealment, and the level that trips the enemy's trip-wire is not written down anywhere.

options.title: Fully Passive
advantages: Bore-well data, registry traffic, and watching survey routes, none of which can trip anything
The cover gets stronger with every honest filing
The analysis narrows steadily: 30 to 40 days to a single candidate at current data rates
disadvantages: 30 to 40 days against a {STORM_DAYS}-day season leaves no margin
The raids continue the whole time, charged to your patience at the employer's table
Passive data alone may never reach the two-source standard; narrowing it down is not the same as confirming it
options.consequence: The quiet road, at the mercy of the season. If the storm comes early or the math lands late, the hunt ends with a strong suspicion, an intact cover, and no fee.

costs.resource: the storm margin: 30-40 of {STORM_DAYS} days spent narrowing it down
costs.risk: the season beats the analysis, and a strongest-candidate-but-unconfirmed result is worth exactly 40 percent of the contract

options.title: One Active Probe
advantages: A 6-person recon of the best candidate over 5 nights: eyes on the ground, the best evidence there is
If it goes clean and the candidate is right, that is your first confirmation source in under a week
The probe team also collects the pattern-of-life data for the bonus objective
disadvantages: Detection starts the 72-hour clock against the whole contract
The Maze favors whoever has lived in it: their counter-recon knows the chalk, yours knows the manual
A probe of the wrong candidate spends the risk and buys nothing
options.consequence: One sharp question asked quietly. Answered, it halves the problem. Overheard, it ends the hunt on a 72-hour clock the team in the chalk learns about last.

costs.resource: the unit's best recon element exposed for 5 nights beyond support range
costs.risk: detection starts the 72-hour relocation clock while your team is still inside the site's security radius

options.title: Lace the Supply Channel
advantages: The employer holds a captured Blakist supply contact: tagged goods, such as marked lubricants and doped flour, pushed through it travel to the site on their own
No unit presence anywhere near the candidates
If the tagged goods reach a hearth, that is your first confirmation source, with a clear trail
disadvantages: If the contact is a ROM plant, the hunt has just announced itself by name
The tagged goods take 2 to 3 weeks to arrive, the slowest of the three clocks
The channel handles one shipment, and a wasted load cannot be re-run inside the season
options.consequence: Clever, slow, and balanced on one question nobody can answer: who is really running whom through the contact. The tagged goods arrive at a hearth, or at a ROM counterintelligence desk with your contract attached.

costs.resource: the captured supply contact: a one-use strategic asset, spent on this hunt whatever happens
costs.risk: if it is a plant, the blacklist clause has your name pre-typed and the employer's two prior burns as precedent

decisionPoints.name: One Source Short
decisionPoints.context: The evidence rests on a single source, the dust storm is {STORM_DAYS} days out and closing, and the strike package commits only once. Now the contract's hard numbers become a real decision.

options.title: Call the Strike on One Source
advantages: If it is right, the raids end this season and three systems' logistics get a break
The employer has signaled it would accept one source at a reduced fee, 15 percent down
No more collection risk, and the cover retires clean
disadvantages: One source is exactly how the employer got burned twice, so expect the proposal read in that light
If it is wrong: contract void, blacklist, damages, and the site relocates on the strike's own warning
The 15 percent cut prices doubt, not effort, so the unit eats the difference either way
options.consequence: The bet is the unit's name against a single stream of evidence. Right, and the fee cut is a rounding error on a finished contract. Wrong, and the blacklist does what blacklists do.

costs.resource: fee: 15 percent cut accepted for committing on one source
costs.risk: the whole downside, void and damages and blacklist, riding on one go or no-go signature: yours

options.title: Hold for the Second Source
advantages: Meets the contract's standard as written: full fee, no cut, no argument
Every extra day of bore-well data sharpens the picture anyway
The strike package commits against certainty, the way its owners prefer
disadvantages: 8 to 14 more days of collection at current rates, against a storm that will not wait
The raids continue: one, maybe two more strikes land while you verify
If the season closes first, the evidence you held loses value over the winter as the site relocates on its normal cycle
options.consequence: Professional patience, priced by the weather. The full fee waits at the end of a window that is closing from both sides, and how long that window is, is only an estimate.

costs.resource: storm margin: 8-14 days of a closing season spent on verification
costs.risk: the season closes at one source, and the strongest hunt of the war files as an unconfirmed assessment and a 40 percent invoice

options.title: Spend the Human Source
advantages: The employer holds a captured Blakist supply clerk whose debrief can back up a candidate within 48 hours
The fastest path to a second source: the fee standard met this week
The clerk's information also fills out the pattern-of-life package
disadvantages: Using the debrief openly tells the Word their clerk talked, so the contact network that produced your candidate list dies within a month
The employer's other hunts on other worlds draw from that same network, so your confirmation is billed to their whole collection effort
The clerk's reliability is interrogation-grade: it backs up a candidate, it does not prove one, and everyone signing knows it
options.consequence: You buy the second source out of the employer's own seed corn. The fee pays this season, and the network that would have found the next five hearths, on the next five worlds, stops existing.

costs.resource: the employer's contact network: spent for one corroboration, with every dependent hunt repriced
costs.risk: political: the employer's intelligence directorate notes which contractor spent its network, and directorates outlast contracts

entries.event: The site's counter-recon detects collection: a team spotted, a sensor found, or bore-well data tampering noticed.
A security patrol heads toward the detection point, an estimated one 'Mech lance plus mounted infantry, investigating rather than pursuing.
Exposed elements are either clear of the Maze or in a fight the contract forbids, because the survey cover cannot explain a firefight.
If the suspicion holds, the site starts preparing to relocate: heat bloom, convoy forming up, the one stretch when the site is loud.
Relocation complete. The candidate list is dead, the season is shorter, and the hunt starts over from the retainer.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: Confirm the site before the dust season closes, in {STORM_DAYS} days, or it winters out of reach and the spring raids are as good as already paid for. And from any tripwire event, 72 hours is the only deadline left: act inside it with whatever is ready, or start over from the retainer, with less trust than before.

opforSketch.composition: Hidden site garrison: estimated 200-280 personnel; security element of one BattleMech lance and one vehicle lance (Veteran); counter-reconnaissance teams of 4-6 (Elite) on light vehicles with chalk-country fieldcraft. Generator should keep the garrison invisible until provoked and overwhelming only in the displacement window.
opforSketch.behavior: Detection-averse: sorties investigate and turn back at 20 kilometers, every time — pursuit reveals more than it catches, and they know it. The site's weapon is displacement, not battle. Counter-recon prefers capturing collection equipment intact: what you were looking at tells them what you know.

forks.name: OPERATION SPENT MATCH
forks.trigger: Dual-source confirmation delivered inside the season; strike package commits.
forks.consequence: The unit guides the strike in and takes the cutoff positions on the displacement routes its own analysis mapped — the contract's quiet final clause, and the first time in the hunt anyone wants you to be loud.

forks.name: OPERATION LONG SCENT
forks.trigger: The site displaces unconfirmed, or the season closes at one source.
forks.consequence: The hunt resumes after the storms on a fresh candidate list, a thinner fee, and an employer whose patience is now itself single-source. The raids resume first.

forks.name: OPERATION PULLED STAKE
forks.trigger: The survey cover is blown — registry flag, captured sensor, or the dangle scenario confirmed.
forks.consequence: The site's counter-intelligence sweep rolls up everything the cover touched: three scattered sensor teams, the cover company's local staff, and a registry clerk who asked the wrong favor. Seventy-two hours to extract them all from a continent that has started looking back.

storyElementSeed: A survey tech logs bore seven's evening draw — the same figure as yesterday, the same as the day before. Then she stops, thumbs back nine pages, and reads the night flows again with a torch held in her teeth, and does not put the logbook down for an hour.

is-davion.situation.framing: The proof standard is the mission. Two sources or it did not happen, not because the first source is wrong, but because the strike commits once and the officer authorizing it has been burned twice. Treat certainty as the deliverable and the clock as the enemy's weapon, and write every assessment as if a board of inquiry reads it next week. It might.

STORM_DAYS.unit: days until the dust season closes collection

resourceGates.lackingText: Without depot access, you have no tagging materials, so the option is locked. The employer can ship them in 16 days, a real offer, but accepting it spends the storm margin.

skeleton: hunters must reduce five candidate sites to one proven base with collection quiet enough not to trip a 72-hour relocation reflex, under a season that will blind every sensor and a fee that pays only for certainty
inspiration: the coalition Scud hunt, western desert, 1991

title: OPERATION FIRST CIRCUIT
situation:
The {WORLD} hyperpulse generator has been dark to our side since the schism, and useful to the enemy every day since: blocked to coalition traffic, transmitting only what the Protectorate allows. The sector offensive needs the relay working by day {OFFENSIVE_DAYS}, or three task forces launch coordinating by courier boat, which means on faith, with a six-day message lag. The Precentor Martial's staff has run the numbers on offensives coordinated by faith. Those numbers are why you are reading this.

The station is the Caldera Bowl compound: a transmission complex on the floor of an extinct volcano, reached by one road through the Pilgrim's Notch, with rim positions overlooking every approach for 9 kilometers. A derelict observatory funicular climbs the outer slope to a service gate on the rim: rated for 2.5 tons, 11 minutes per trip up, 4 troops per car. On this ground you can have weight or surprise, but not both, and each part of the plan has to pick one.

Be clear on what the objective is and is not. There is no demolition charge on the core, because ROM does not trust fuses near something it values this much. The order to destroy it is a procedure instead: a 14-minute manual sequence run in the core chamber, which any of the 4 authorized duty officers can perform. From the moment any alarm sounds, each of those four officers is a walking 14-minute countdown. Keep all four out of the chamber and the core survives, by definition.

And the core is the easier half of the job. The station staff, 31 adepts and acolytes of the old Order forced into Blakist service in {YEAR}, are the only people within 40 light-years who can restart a core, and our own two qualified techs are 11 weeks' travel away. The staff's families, 74 people, live in Residence Row in the district town, 7 kilometers down the valley, under a Protectorate political office that keeps attendance records. That threat to their families is the station's real hold on them, and it has to be broken in the same hour you take the station. The Row's duty signaler reports in every hour, and a missed report alerts the station within 60 minutes. Last, the truth the operational annex states once, plainly: a restart crew working under coercion can sabotage a core in ways no instrument check will catch for six weeks. {NPC:employer-contact} personally trained two of the people on that transmission floor. Both sides of this fight came from the same Order. The prize is not the machine. The prize is 31 people choosing to run it.

objectives.primary: Take the station with the core intact, letting no authorized officer finish the destruction sequence, and secure Residence Row within the same alarm cycle.
objectives.secondary: Win the staff's freely given cooperation: they restart the core themselves and transmit verified coalition traffic by day {OFFENSIVE_DAYS}.
objectives.bonus: Capture the interdiction-era traffic logs intact, because they record which stations passed Blakist traffic willingly, an audit the Order owes itself.

complications.name: The Procedure
complications.text: Four officers, one sequence, fourteen minutes. There is nothing to defuse and nothing to cut, only people to keep out of a room.
complications.mechanicalEffect: From any alarm, track all 4 authorized officers. Any officer who gets 14 minutes alone in the core chamber ends the primary objective for good. Seizing the chamber, or accounting for all 4 officers, ends the threat.

complications.name: The Rim Sees Everything
complications.text: A vehicle approach through the Notch is spotted 9 kilometers out, giving at least 25 minutes of warning. The funicular carries only 4 troops per 11-minute cycle. This ground offers stealth or weight, never both.
complications.mechanicalEffect: A Notch approach gives the defense 25 minutes to prepare. Funicular infiltration moves 4 troops per 11 minutes with a 2.5-ton lift limit: no battle armor over that weight, and no support weapons heavier than man-portable.

complications.name: Residence Row
complications.text: The Row's political office reports to the station every hour. Both objectives share one alarm link, and that link is one clerk with a schedule.
complications.mechanicalEffect: A missed hourly report from the Row alerts the station within 60 minutes, and a station alarm triggers the Row's relocation protocol within 40. You must start both objectives inside the same reporting cycle, or each one warns the other.

complications.name: The Staff Are Kin
complications.text: The people at the consoles are the Order's own, whatever insignia the occupation sewed on them. In the only judgment that decides the secondary objective, theirs, every casualty among them turns a rescue into a raid.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Staff casualties from your fire stack up as penalties on the cooperation outcome at decision point two. Zero staff casualties is a stated planning requirement, not a hope.

decisionPoints.name: The Order of Operations
decisionPoints.context: Two objectives, 7 kilometers apart, sharing one alarm link. The order you choose decides which clock starts first, and every clock in this valley is short.

options.title: Both at Once
advantages: No warning travels either way, because both alarm paths are cut in the same minutes
The Row's families and the station's officers are each secured before either knows about the other
The cleanest version of the night, if it works
disadvantages: Both teams are understrength: the funicular feeds the station team only 4 troops per 11 minutes while the valley team works the Row
The window to sync the two attacks is 8 minutes wide and depends on a derelict funicular motor
No reserve: whoever is already there has to handle every surprise
options.consequence: Either everything happens at once or nothing does. What makes the plan brilliant is exactly what makes it fragile, and all of it rides on a cable car built for astronomers.

costs.resource: force split: neither team above 60 percent of the strength its task needs
costs.risk: the funicular motor: one mechanical failure mid-cycle strands half the station team on a cliff face at H-hour

options.title: Residence Row First
advantages: The families are physically safe before any station alarm can happen
The valley team works at full strength against the lighter objective
The hold over the staff breaks first: whatever happens next, the political office has lost its leverage
disadvantages: The Row's missed hourly report alerts the station within 60 minutes, so the infiltration team must already be through the rim gate when the signal stops
Sixty minutes sounds like a lot until you measure it against 4 officers and 14 minutes
If the station alarm beats the infiltration, the raid becomes an assault on a warned rim
options.consequence: You solve the hostage problem first and make the station problem harder by exactly one missed phone call. The infiltration team's timetable pays for the difference.

costs.resource: the 60-minute report window: the station assault's entire surprise budget, spent in advance
costs.risk: a 14-minute procedure fits inside a 60-minute warning four times over, so the only margin is officer confusion, not the clock

options.title: Station First, Row by Speed
advantages: Full strength against the harder objective: you can seal the core chamber before any officer reaches it
You can keep the station's fall off the air for a useful stretch, so the Row learns late
The funicular infiltration gets every capable specialist instead of half
disadvantages: On a station alarm, the political office's standing order is relocation: the families load onto trucks for the district fort within 40 minutes
The race down-valley is run with whatever the station assault has left
The 31 will be watching the valley road, not the consoles, so their cooperation waits on news of the Row, and that news is a truck convoy
options.consequence: You secure the machine, but the people who must run it stand at the windows. Whether the raid won anything is decided 7 kilometers away, by a road race the plan scheduled last.

costs.resource: the relocation race: 40 minutes against trucks, run by whatever the assault has left
costs.risk: the families reach the district fort, so the hold over the staff survives the raid intact, now held by people who know exactly what it is worth

decisionPoints.name: What the Staff Are Owed
decisionPoints.context: The core is taken; the consoles wait. Thirty-one people who have spent years under one set of masters now weigh the new set. The honest restart is theirs to give or withhold.

options.title: Ask, Face to Face
advantages: {NPC:employer-contact} goes in with the first element, unarmored, to speak Order to Order
If they believe it, cooperation comes at once and complete, the strongest restart on the fastest clock
The gesture itself is proof: the coalition sent someone who knows their names, not a requisition form
disadvantages: The one person the restart depends on most is risked in the breach, first
Belief is not a plan: years under ROM teach people to read sincerity as a trick
If they refuse, the refusal is public and personal, and every later approach starts from there
options.consequence: The Order asks its own people to come home, in person, at the moment of greatest fear. Everything after this, the restart, the offensive, the audit, flows from what those 31 people decide in that room about one familiar face.

costs.resource: {NPC:employer-contact} committed to the assault echelon, the mission's irreplaceable asset placed at its point of highest risk
costs.risk: a stray round or a ROM holdout in the first ten minutes turns the appeal into a martyrdom and the restart into a negotiation with the grieving

options.title: Terms in Writing
advantages: Evacuation for all 31 plus the 74, stipends, resettlement, and the employer's seal on every page
Cooperation becomes a contract: durable, auditable, and safe from second thoughts on both sides
The staff has families to think of, and the terms put those families first, which the staff will notice
disadvantages: 380,000 C-bills plus lift commitments, against a treasury that also has an offensive to fund
Negotiation takes days the offensive clock will not spare
The staff knows exactly the difference between being valued and being priced, and the paper shows which this is
options.consequence: Cooperation bought honestly is still bought. The relay restarts on schedule or close to it, run by professionals fulfilling terms, and the loyalty is exactly as good as professional, which the annex says is good enough. Probably.

costs.resource: lift commitment: 105 evacuees on coalition transport inside the offensive's loading schedule
costs.risk: the terms leak to ROM stay-behinds in the district, and 105 named people become targets in transit, under your escort

options.title: Verification Instead of Trust
advantages: Restart under full instrument audit, with the two distant techs reviewing readings by relay at each stage
No reliance on goodwill, gratitude, or anyone's read of anyone's heart
The procedure holds up to every staff section that has never met an adept
disadvantages: Nine days instead of two, against an offensive clock of {OFFENSIVE_DAYS} days
The staff reads exactly what the instruments mean: they are suspects with consoles
Audited people align cores exactly as well as the audit can detect, which is the original problem again with better paperwork
options.consequence: Trust gives way to instrument readings, and the readings are honest about everything except intention. The relay comes up slowly and certified, and the one question the audit cannot answer rides every transmission of the offensive.

costs.resource: offensive margin: 9 of {OFFENSIVE_DAYS} days spent on staged verification
costs.risk: the six-week failure mode: a sabotage no instrument catches, surfacing mid-offensive with three task forces relying on its traffic

entries.event: Station alarm, from any source: a sentry contact, a funicular gate breach, or the Row's missed report arriving on its own path.
Duty board check: 2 authorized officers on the transmission floor, 1 in quarters, 1 elsewhere. Security teams move to seal the core chamber approaches, racing yours with different maps.
Earliest the destruction sequence can finish, if any officer reached the chamber at the alarm. The primary objective now comes down to which doors held.
Rim positions fully manned and the Notch road closed. Whatever has not entered the caldera is not getting in.
Residence Row's reporting cycle runs out: whichever objective you did not start is now warned, and its protocol, destruction or relocation, is running.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: The offensive's coordination traffic flows by day {OFFENSIVE_DAYS}, or three task forces launch on courier lag. Behind that public clock sits the private one: from any alarm, 14 minutes alone in the core chamber and the relay becomes a monument. There is no second relay in this sector. There is no second staff anywhere.

opforSketch.composition: Station security: one Word of Blake Level II of mixed BattleMechs and battle armor (Veteran) plus 2 infantry platoons on rim positions. Residence Row: political office detachment — 1 infantry platoon, 2 light vehicles (Regular). The 4 authorized officers are objectives with legs, not primarily combatants. Generator should weight the fight toward infantry actions in compound interiors; the Level II is the outer shell.
opforSketch.behavior: Station doctrine is delay toward the core chamber: security fights to buy the procedure its 14 minutes, not to destroy the raiders. Residence Row doctrine is relocation, not defense. ROM officers will use the staff as passive cover — knowing exactly what staff casualties cost you — and the generator should make that arithmetic visible at the table.

forks.name: OPERATION CLEAR SIGNAL
forks.trigger: Core intact, staff cooperating, relay transmitting coalition traffic.
forks.consequence: The station's first coalition transmission is also its first confession of capture: the counter-raid tasking writes itself at the district fort within hours. The unit that took the relay holds it — through the offensive it just made possible.

forks.name: OPERATION KEPT WORD
forks.trigger: The core is burned out, or the staff's cooperation is refused beyond recovery.
forks.consequence: The relay is a monument and the 31 plus 74 are burned assets the moment the raid touched the valley — ROM's after-action arithmetic is thorough. The evacuation the terms would have promised must happen anyway, unpaid, pursued, and owed.

forks.name: OPERATION SECOND VOICE
forks.trigger: A subtle misalignment surfaces when the relay fails mid-offensive — the six-week failure mode, arrived early.
forks.consequence: Three task forces lose coordination in mid-stride. The nearest alternative relay is one jump out, status unknown, garrison unknown: a reconnaissance to determine what it would cost to ask the same question again, somewhere worse.

storyElementSeed: In a warehouse far from the valley, the infiltration team rehearses the core-chamber corridor with chalk lines on concrete. Fourteen minutes is paced out at a walk, then at a run, then carrying a stretcher. The last rehearsal nobody speaks at all, and it comes in at eleven.

merc.situation.framing: The employer's brief calls the station staff 'human terrain,' which is how institutions say 'people we need who do not work for us.' The bonus structure is more honest: the restart clause pays triple the seizure clause, because the employer knows the machine is the cheap half. Note clause 12: staff casualties void the restart bonus entirely. Someone upstairs did that math in lives first and C-bills second, and for once the contract is the better moral guide.

OFFENSIVE_DAYS.unit: days until the offensive requires the relay

resourceGates.lackingText: Below 400,000 C-bills, the written terms become just the employer's promise to pay later. The staff has spent nine years learning what institutional promises are worth, so the cooperation outcome drops, and the annex will not estimate by how much.

skeleton: raiders must capture a facility whose worth exists only if its operators choose to run it, denying four officers a fourteen-minute destruction procedure while simultaneously freeing the hostage families that guarantee the operators' obedience
inspiration: T-Force seizures of intact technical plant and personnel ahead of scorched-earth orders, Germany 1945

title: OPERATION LAST TRAM
situation:
The strike happened in {YEAR}; the reckoning is now. Someone set off a low-yield warhead over {DISTRICT}'s fusion plant district on {WORLD}. The reactor fires did the rest, throwing up a fallout plume that turned the city's second core into ground you measure in radiation dose, not distance. The coalition radiation survey, revision 3, gives the remaining people {EVAC_DAYS} days before their total exposure crosses the mass-casualty line. The model is four days old, and revision 2 gave six more days than this one, so plan to the worse number, because the model only ever revises one way. The zone holds {ZONE_POP} people by the last pre-strike count, which is the only count there is.

You are contracted to run three decontamination-and-registration portals, NORTH, RAIL, and SOUTH, which can certify at most 6,000 evacuees per day when everything works. The way out is one rail line over the Causeway Viaduct: 11 kilometers raised across salt marsh, damaged by the blast, limited to one 14-car train per 70-minute cycle. Engineering's plan to strengthen it takes 30 days, which the window does not allow. Road convoys along the marsh service track add only 400 to 700 a day, at brutal cost to the vehicles. Set {ZONE_POP} people against 6,000 a day and it barely fits inside {EVAC_DAYS} days. There is almost no slack, and no portal-hour lost can be made up anywhere.

The contract is standard coalition boilerplate from the post-atrocity period, and it is harsh: you are paid per evacuee certified through decontamination, you are liable for any contamination in the clean camps, and clause 22 extends that liability to 'persons certified in error.' Read the threat assessment and you will see why clause 22 exists. A Word of Blake cadre of 30 to 60 people, with a ROM-trained core, has been in the city since before the strike. The assessment's careful phrasing, 'elements displaced into the zone in the 72 hours preceding the strike,' means they knew it was coming. They need to get out, and they cannot pass biometric screening. Their best way out is a broken portal and a surge of panicked people through the wire. Their second-best is a stream of forged certifications running from inside your own process. Expect both to be tried, in that order or together.

Last, the people staying: an estimated {REFUSERS} residents are refusing to leave, pensioners, plant-watch volunteers, and people guarding property that is all they have left. They are owed a policy too, and whatever policy you choose is also the cadre's best long-term hiding place. The Viaduct's three nearest piers are cracking steadily and are monitored hourly. The load limit may drop. It will not rise.

objectives.primary: Certify and lift the zone's willing population before day {EVAC_DAYS}, reaching at least 92 percent of those registered.
objectives.secondary: Zero unscreened crossings: the cadre leaves in custody or not at all.
objectives.bonus: Register, supply, and map the people staying behind, so the follow-on cordon inherits a proper list instead of a rumor.

complications.name: The Viaduct Counts Down
complications.text: Eleven kilometers of cracked concrete carries the whole plan. The pier monitoring is honest, and the news is never good twice in a row.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Weekly pier-integrity rolls. A degraded result drops the limit to 10 cars per train, which reprices throughput at once. Any overload or panic-boarding event risks closing the line entirely.

complications.name: Certified in Error
complications.text: Under clause 22, every cadre member who walks through your portal with clean paper is a liability with your unit's signature on it: found later, billed after the fact, and never forgotten.
complications.mechanicalEffect: The generator logs each cadre-passage event in secret. Confirmed passages surface during the fork phase, bringing contract penalties plus the COMPROMISED fork's conditions.

complications.name: The People Staying
complications.text: Use force on the people staying and you empty the queues of the people going, because the districts watch how you knock on doors. Trust quietly multiplies throughput, and no budget accounts for it.
complications.mechanicalEffect: Door-to-door operations cost 1 platoon per district-day and roll against a trust track. Lost trust thins the voluntary queues at all portals by 10-20 percent the following week.

complications.name: The Model Moves
complications.text: Revisions arrive every 4 to 6 days, and revision 4 will not be kinder than revision 3. Plans built on the hopeful number fail in public.
complications.mechanicalEffect: On each model revision event, the {EVAC_DAYS} deadline may shorten by 1-3 days. Schedules with no slack absorb the change as triage, and the GM applies it to whichever decision the table most recently priced tight.

decisionPoints.name: Throughput Against Integrity
decisionPoints.context: By week two the portals are behind schedule, as they always are, and each of the three ways to catch up means giving up something the contract says is not for sale.

options.title: Cut Screening Depth
advantages: Dropping secondary biometrics to spot-checks raises throughput 40 percent, and the math closes with 2 days to spare
Queue wait times halve, giving the cadre fewer crowd surges to exploit
The medical line gains capacity it badly needs
disadvantages: The cadre's chance of a clean walk rises toward certain, which is clause 22 in slow motion
Forged certifications that full screening would catch now pass at spot-check rates
The decision is on record: when passages surface later, 'the unit chose to cut screening' is the first line of the finding
options.consequence: You meet the deadline and quietly open the wire, by your own decision. Everyone certified gets out, but exactly who got out among them becomes a question for the camps, the inquiry, and the years afterward.

costs.resource: screening integrity: cadre-passage odds rise to near-certain, and clause 22 exposure builds each day
costs.risk: liability after the fact: every confirmed passage is billed against the unit once the contract closes, when the evidence cannot be argued

options.title: Hold Full Screening
advantages: The wire stays clean: you meet the secondary objective by procedure, not luck
Clause 22 exposure stays at the level the contract expected
Every certification you issue survives every later audit
disadvantages: You miss the window by a projected 4 to 6 days at current rates
The extra exposure over those days means an estimated 200 to 400 casualties, stated plainly in the model annex and nowhere else
The employer's reply to your notice arrives after the decision mattered, which is exactly what the brief-and-proceed clause is for
options.consequence: Integrity held, at the price the model names. The unit does the defensible thing and the dose curve does what dose curves do, and both facts go in the same report.

costs.resource: the dose model's margin: 4-6 days past the window, an estimated 200-400 extra casualties carried on the operation's record
costs.risk: the model revises downward mid-decision and the miss grows after the choice is already made

options.title: Fourth Portal, Deputized Staff
advantages: A tram-depot portal staffed by deputized residents under your NCOs adds 25 percent throughput
Local knowledge reads faces that paperwork cannot: the deputies have caught both false identities so far
The districts see their own people running their own exit, and the trust track improves
disadvantages: The cadre may already have deputies of its own, and vetting locals with the records this city has left is barely vetting at all
Favoritism in the line at a neighbor-run portal is certain, visible, and a spark for a riot
Your NCOs stretch across four sites, thinning supervision exactly where the new risk is highest
options.consequence: You recruit the city into its own evacuation, with everything that buys and everything it costs. The fourth portal is the fastest and the least under your control, in equal measure.

costs.resource: NCO supervision stretched across four sites, with deputy vetting admittedly minimal
costs.risk: a cadre-owned deputy is a forged-certification stream with a coalition stamp, the cadre's second-best exit, staffed by your own signature

decisionPoints.name: The Last Districts
decisionPoints.context: Three days before the window closes, two districts and the people staying are still here. How you spend the final days is what this operation will be remembered for, and that gets decided now.

options.title: Compulsory Clearance
advantages: The window is met to the letter: nobody's grandmother is left to the dose curve by her own bad math
The medical annex backs it fully, because the model does not care about consent
The follow-on cordon inherits an empty city, the cleanest possible handover
disadvantages: Troops carrying pensioners out of apartments, filmed from every window that still has glass, and that imagery follows the unit into every future contract talk
Resistance eats the final days' escort capacity: each forced district costs throughput the willing queues needed
The clause covering 'involuntary relocation outcomes' is vague, and vagueness in a liability contract always resolves against the signer
options.consequence: Everyone leaves, which was the mission. How they leave is what gets remembered, which is the cost. The dose curve is beaten by force, with the unit as the force.

costs.resource: final-days throughput: 30-40 percent of escort capacity pulled off certification to force people out
costs.risk: one violent incident in a stairwell, filmed, becomes the operation's public name

options.title: Final-Notice Protocol
advantages: A published last tram, a 6-hour hold at the platform, and departure on schedule: the contract's letter met exactly
No images of forced removals, and the trust track holds for the willing queues' final surge
Whoever stays, stays by documented choice, so the legal position is clean
disadvantages: The record is also {REFUSERS} people, and it will be read aloud someday with the casualty model next to it
The cadre's patient remainder simply waits among the people staying for the cordon to lose interest
The 6-hour hold is the operation's last big crowd, and the cadre's final and best-rehearsed window
options.consequence: The last tram leaves full, on time, with empty seats held to the final minute. What stays behind stays by choice, and the operation's conscience is filed away as paperwork.

costs.risk: the 6-hour platform hold gathers the largest crowd of the operation at its most weakly screened moment

options.title: Stay-Behind Compact
advantages: Registered residents, supply caches, marked shelters, and 72 hours of radiation-safety training: the bonus objective achieved as policy
The people staying become wardens of the empty districts instead of obstacles in them
The follow-on cordon inherits names, addresses, and a working relationship
disadvantages: The compact makes official the very thing the evacuation exists to prevent, with your stamp on the ration cards
A recognized stay-behind community is the cadre's best long-term shelter, so the secondary and bonus objectives collide here, in writing
The medical annex formally objects, and that objection stays in the contract file forever
options.consequence: You buy order inside the zone by admitting the zone is still inhabited. It is humane and organized, and the cleanest gift the cadre's patient men will ever be handed.

costs.resource: 72 hours of training and cache logistics in the final week, taken from the lift schedule's margin
costs.risk: the compact's registry becomes the cadre's cover documents, so your bonus objective doubles as their false identities

entries.event: Portal attack alarm at the RAIL portal, matching the pattern the assessment predicted.
The crowd compresses at the wire: the barrier line takes casualties from crowd pressure before any order is given.
The clean lane holds or it is breached: 200-plus unscreened into the marsh approaches is the cadre's big move, and the marsh has no second wire.
The portal reopens at a reduced rate, or the day's roughly 2,000 certifications are gone from a plan that had no spare 2,000.
The next train. The Viaduct does not wait, and empty seats on a 70-minute cycle are the one truly unforgivable waste.

reactionTimeline.hardDeadline: On day {EVAC_DAYS} the dose model crosses its line, and the contract's window closes with it. Work backward from there: any portal dark more than 18 hours, or the Viaduct at 10 cars for more than a week, and no later effort makes up the difference. The model does not negotiate, and neither do the piers.

opforSketch.composition: Word of Blake cadre: 30-60 effectives — ROM-trained core of 8-12 (Elite), remainder Regular — with smallarms, breaching charges, 2-3 civilian vehicles, and possibly one cached battle armor suit (UNCONFIRMED — basis: pre-strike power-cell purchases traced to a zone address). Generator should produce infantry-scale incidents against process infrastructure, never a stand-up fight.
opforSketch.behavior: The cadre fights the process, not the unit: portal attacks timed to peak queues, forged-certification probes, rumor seeding among refusers and deputies. It needs chaos at a portal exactly once, and it will spend weeks buying that minute. Direct engagement means it has already failed and is spending itself on spite — which the ROM core, notably, will not do while an exit remains.

forks.name: OPERATION VACANT WATCH
forks.trigger: Evacuation completed inside the window; no confirmed unscreened crossings.
forks.consequence: The emptied city becomes the cordon, and the cadre still inside becomes the only population that moves after dark. The follow-on contract is the hunt through a city of empty windows — with the refuser ledger (if it exists) as the only map of who belongs.

forks.name: OPERATION THIN BLANKET
forks.trigger: The window is missed by 4+ days, or a breach event floods the camps with unscreened arrivals.
forks.consequence: The camp system breaks where the city did not: over capacity, under screened, and angry in the specific way of people who did everything asked of them. The unit's contract extension is crowd lines at the ration points it built.

forks.name: OPERATION CENSUS GHOST
forks.trigger: Cadre passage through the portals is confirmed after certification.
forks.consequence: Between 6 and 20 cadre hold clean camp registrations among 100,000 genuine victims. Finding them is collection work conducted in ration queues and tent rows — every method that might work is a method applied to people the operation just finished saving.

storyElementSeed: At Portal 2 a decon line worker chalks a number on each suitcase and the same number on its owner's wrist. When the train doors close she counts the chalk stubs left in the box, writes the count in a school notebook, and starts sharpening for tomorrow.

is-steiner.situation.framing: The Commonwealth measures relief in tonnage and timetables, because tonnage and timetables are the only mercy that scales; compassion without rolling stock behind it is just a speech. The three numbers that matter are the Viaduct cycle, the portal ceiling, and the dose model. Put your attention on whichever of the three is currently lying, and one of them always is.

EVAC_DAYS.unit: days until the dose model crosses the mass-casualty line

ZONE_POP.unit: persons in the affected zone (pre-strike count)

resourceGates.lackingText: With no depot access, the decontamination supplies for a fourth lane have to come from the existing three, so the net throughput gain drops from 25 percent to 10, while the vetting and favoritism risks stay at full price.

skeleton: evacuation force must move a poisoned city through fixed-throughput screening before a dose-model deadline while an embedded enemy needs the screening to fail in order to leave inside the crowd
inspiration: the Pripyat evacuation, 1986, crossed with displaced-persons screening, 1945
